1.title: On CBS: Chairman Moolenaar Confronts China on Taiwan, Iran, Russia, and AI Export Controls
1.description:
House Select Committee on China Chairman Rep. John Moolenaar joins CBS News and outlines U.S. strategy toward China, Taiwan, and advanced technology. 

-He discusses the pending $14 billion arms sale to Taiwan, China’s growing aggression in the region, and Xi Jinping’s stated goal of “reunification” by force by 2027. 
- Moolenaar explains President Trump’s approach to hosting Xi Jinping—combining respect with firm messages on China’s support for Iran and Russia, fentanyl precursors, and economic leverage. 
- He also details why the U.S. must maintain strong export controls on advanced chips and chip‑making equipment, reduce dependence on Chinese rare earth minerals, and work with allies to prevent China from achieving exponential gains in AI and military‑relevant technologies.

2.title: Moolenaar on BBC: Taiwan Tensions, Iran & Russia Ties, and AI Chip Controls
2.description:
Chairman Rep. Moolenaar, Chair of the House Select Committee on China, joins the BBC to discuss U.S.–China relations during President Trump’s meeting with Xi Jinping.

He addresses:
-U.S. commitment to the status quo in the Taiwan Strait and concerns over Chinese military threats to Taiwan, Japan, and the Philippines
-China’s support for Iran and Russia, including its role in backing Russia’s war in Ukraine
-Efforts to block China’s access to advanced AI chips, including a “rolling technical threshold” and cooperation with partners like the EU, ASML, and TSMC

Rep. Moolenaar underscores the need for a respectful diplomatic tone while firmly defending U.S. national security interests and those of our allies.

3.title: Rep. John Moolenaar: Confronting China on AI, Taiwan, Iran, and Rising Costs at Home
3.description:
Rep. John Moolenaar (R-MI), Chairman of the House Select Committee on China, joins NewsNation to discuss U.S.–China relations as Xi visits the United States.

In this interview, Rep. Moolenaar covers:

- Diplomacy with China: Why the U.S. must balance hospitality and respect with tough, direct conversations about Beijing’s role in global instability.
- Taiwan & Regional Security: The importance of maintaining the status quo in the Taiwan Strait and deterring aggression toward Taiwan, Japan, and the Philippines.
Iran & Russia: Concerns over China assisting Iran and Russia, including materials that can be used militarily and threaten American servicemembers.
- AI & Advanced Chips: Why Moolenaar supports strict export controls on advanced U.S. chips and AI technologies to protect national security, and where limited trade may still make sense.
- Diesel Prices & American Families: How regional conflicts and Iran policy intersect with rising diesel prices, and what that means for farmers and working families.

4.title: Moolenaar: The CCP's Role in Iran’s Attacks Against the U.S.
4.description: Ahead of President Trump’s meeting with Xi Jinping, Select Committee Chairman Rep. Moolenaar warns that China’s role in Iran’s attacks against the U.S. must be a priority.

5.title: Meet Xi Jinping
5.description: The biggest opponent of freedom and liberty in the world. Wherever he goes and no matter where he is, Xi will always be the CCP leader behind some of the world’s cruelest human rights abuses.

6.title: China is fueling Iran’s attacks on U.S. military assets.
6.description: Xi Jinping is Iran’s number one enabler in its ongoing war against the United States. Watch this video to learn how China is fueling Iran’s attacks on U.S. military assets.

7.title: Stopping CCP Leverage: A New Strategy for U.S. Import Controls
7.description:
Peter Harrell testifies before the Select Committee on China on how the U.S. should use national security import controls to reduce dangerous dependencies on China. 

He explains the current fragmented legal framework, warns that bans alone don’t eliminate cyber and espionage threats, and uses drones, Huawei/ZTE, and Chinese connected vehicles as key examples. Harrell urges Congress to establish a systematic risk assessment process, give these tools a durable statutory footing, pair controls with industrial policy and cybersecurity standards, and work closely with allies to build secure, alternative supply chains and a combined market capable of competing with China.

8.title: Breaking CCP Control: Oren Cass on Ending U.S. Dependence on China
8.description: In this hearing before the House Select Committee on China, Oren Cass warns that the Chinese Communist Party is weaponizing trade and industrial policy to dominate strategic sectors, hollow out U.S. industry, and create dangerous American dependencies. He argues that economic relations with China are fundamentally asymmetric, with Chinese firms operating as extensions of the state, and calls for bold import controls, a default of “no interaction” in critical sectors, and urgent passage of measures like the Connected Vehicle Security Act and the Guard Act to protect U.S. economic sovereignty and national security.

9.title: FDD’s Singleton Warns of CCP Threat to America’s Supply Chain Security and Dominance
9.description:
Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD) expert Craig Singleton testifies before the House Select Committee on China about the growing threat posed by the Chinese Communist Party (CCP).

He explains how Beijing’s industrial strategy, from Made in China 2025 to its new five-year plan, is designed to build “technology beachheads” in key sectors—drones, batteries, chips, sensors, industrial equipment, and more—giving China leverage over the U.S. in a crisis.

Craig urges Congress to:

•Create a doctrine for inbound tech to keep high-risk Chinese technologies out of critical systems
•Move from case-by-case bans to sector-wide controls that follow entire supply chains
•Strengthen FCC and federal procurement authorities so taxpayer dollars don’t fund high risk Chinese tech
•Build clear pathways for trusted allied technologies from Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, and others to scale in the U.S. market

10.title: Opening Statement | Chairman Moolenaar on Import Controls and CCP Supply Chain Security Threats
10.description: Chairman John Moolenaar led a Select Committee on China hearing examining import controls on Chinese products and how the United States can strengthen relevant authorities to advance supply chains and safeguard national and economic security in critical sectors.

11.title: Rep. Newhouse: Using Import Controls to End U.S. Dependence on China
11.description:
House Select Committee on China Member Rep. Dan Newhouse presses expert witnesses on how the U.S. can use import controls to secure long-term supply chain dominance and reduce dangerous dependencies on China.

Witnesses outline:

•Why it’s far easier to prevent new dependencies than to unwind entrenched supply chains
•How a national “import vulnerability survey” could map critical U.S. reliance on China
•The need to move quickly on emerging sectors—like humanoid robots—before China locks in dominance
•Why phased reductions in Chinese imports must be paired with strong U.S. industrial policy and financing
•How Beijing’s own plans (e.g., Made in China 2025) reveal a roadmap for where it intends to entangle the United States

12.title: Rep. Hinson on Ending U.S. Reliance on China for Critical Drug Ingredients
12.description:
China controls 70–90% of the global supply of key pharmaceutical inputs, leaving American families dangerously dependent on the CCP for essential medicines and even infant formula ingredients.

House Select Committee on China Member, Rep. Ashley Hinson, presses Oren Cass of American Compass on the policy tools Congress needs to:
• Onshore and friend-shore active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) production
• Strengthen transparency through efforts like the Drug Origin Transparency Act
• Use targeted import controls to reduce reliance on China
• Rebuild U.S. manufacturing capacity and partner with trusted allies

Rep. Hinson makes clear: Americans deserve safe, reliable, and transparent access to medicines—and the United States must not be dependent on the CCP for critical pharmaceutical supply chains.

13.title: Import Controls: Tools to Counter the CCP's Industrial Policy and Supply Chain Threats
13.description:
Witnesses:
- Mr. Craig Singleton, China Senior Director, The Foundation for Defense of Democracies
- Mr. Oren Cass, Founder and Chief Economist, American Compass
- Mr. Peter Harrell, Visiting Scholar, Georgetown University Institute of International Economic Law; Senior Fellow, Council on Foreign Relations

14.title: The CCP is trying to control the selection of the next Dalai Lama.
14.description: Watch to learn how the CCP is trying to control the selection of the next Dalai Lama.

15.title: The History of Tibet
15.description: This is the history of Tibet the CCP wants people to forget.

16.title: Pastor Jin Exposes CCP Persecution of Christians
16.description: Pastor Jin recently shared the details of his unlawful detainment by the Chinese Communist Party. His testimony is a stark reminder of the persecution Christians face under the CCP.

17.title: Two U.S. citizens helped the CCP threaten and intimidate dissidents on U.S. soil.
17.description: Two U.S. citizens ran an overseas Chinese police station in America, helping the CCP threaten and intimidate dissidents on U.S. soil. Congress must pass the Transnational Repression Policy Act to stop CCP harassment in America.

18.title: The Risks of Chinese Robotics in U.S. Innovation
18.description: Michael Robbins of Association for Uncrewed Vehicle Systems International (AUVSI) supports Chairman Rep. Moolenaar’s bipartisan GUARD Act and warns that allowing Chinese robotics to dominate would put U.S. innovation at risk.

19.title: Congress Must Pass Moolenaar's Bipartisan GUARD Act
19.description: To boost American robotics, Congress must pass Chairman Rep. Moolenaar’s bipartisan GUARD Act. This would require the U.S. government to check Chinese robots for national security risks, automatically block Chinese military linked robots from the U.S, and remove adversarial robotics out of our sensitive manufacturing lines.

20.title: America’s AI Edge & China’s Pharma Risks: Rep. Moolenaar on Fox Business
20.description:
House Select Committee on China Chairman Rep. John Moolenaar joins Fox Business to discuss:

- How the U.S. can keep its lead in advanced AI chips while China’s exports surge
- Why we must limit sales of high‑end semiconductors that fuel Beijing’s military and surveillance state
- The committee’s investigation into Merck, AbbVie, Eli Lilly, Pfizer, and Bristol Myers Squibb over clinical trials in China, including Xinjiang and PLA hospitals
- Ethical concerns about informed consent, data security, and CCP access to American biopharmaceutical innovation
- The urgent need to end U.S. dependence on China for critical medicines and bring supply chains and manufacturing back to America

Learn more about the Select Committee's pharmaceutical company investigation: https://chinaselectcommittee.house.gov/issues/biosecurity

21.title: Protecting American Innovation: The Federal Research Security Enterprise
21.description:
Witnesses:
- Mr. Jeremy Ison, Chief of Staff to the Under Secretary for Science, U.S. Department of Energy
- Dr. Patricia Valdez, Chief Extramural Research Integrity Officer, National Institutes of Health
- Dr. Rebecca Keiser, Acting Chief of Staff and Chief of Research Security Policy and Strategy, National Science Foundation

22.title: Rep. Nunn Exposes CCP Threat to America’s Food Supply & Praises $160M NSF Bio-Grant
22.description:
Rep. Zach Nunn highlights how a new $160 million NSF Rural Stamina Biomanufacturing Engineering Grant is turning federal research in Iowa and Nebraska into world-class bio-innovation—while warning that the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) is working to steal it.

He also highlights:
•$160M NSF Rural Stamina biomanufacturing investment in Iowa & Nebraska
•How federal research becomes real-world jobs and innovation in the rural heartland
•CCP attempts to steal U.S. agricultural technology and exploit our supply chain
•Recent CCP-linked plots to smuggle pathogens and potential agro-terror weapons
•Rep. Nunn’s PLANT Act to hold CCP-linked actors accountable
•The need to extend research security beyond university gates and into commercialization

23.title: Protecting Taxpayer-Funded Research: Rep. Newhouse Demands Clear Commitments
23.description:
Rep. Newhouse questions witnesses on how the U.S. is protecting taxpayer-funded research from theft by the Chinese Communist Party and other adversaries.

In his line of questioning, he also: 
•Asks what critical know-how and talent the U.S. has already lost to the PRC
•Presses witnesses for a clear commitment to implement the new NSF–DoD policy restricting research collaboration with “bad actor” entities
•Highlights the stakes for facilities like Pacific Northwest National Laboratory in his district
•Challenges DOE on how it uses tools like the S&T risk matrix, talent program prohibitions, and enhanced vetting to secure research while still allowing commercialization

24.title: Rep. Hinson Demands Stronger Vetting to Keep CCP Out of U.S. Energy Research
24.description:
Rep. Ashley Hinson presses Department of Energy (DOE) official Mr. Ison on how DOE is protecting federally funded research from Chinese Communist Party influence, including at Ames National Laboratory in Iowa. 

Rep. Hinson highlights the importance of securing America’s energy future, safeguarding critical and rare earth mineral research, and tightening vetting of foreign nationals—especially those linked to the Chinese military and CCP-backed talent programs. 

Mr. Ison outlines DOE’s current security framework, counterintelligence efforts, and new risk management and escalation procedures, as Hinson pushes for stronger protections to keep malign actors out and ensure the United States remains competitive and secure.

25.title: Rep. LaHood Presses DOE on Protecting U.S. Research from CCP Theft
25.description:
Rep. Darin LaHood (IL) questions Department of Energy (DOE) official on how the DOE is protecting U.S. taxpayer-funded research from exploitation by the CCP.

Rep. LaHood underscores how the CCP:
•Uses IP theft, forced technology transfers, and coercive trade tactics
•Targets AI, quantum, and advanced chip manufacturing
•Exploits U.S. academic institutions and national labs to acquire sensitive know-how

He highlights the COINS Act, passed by Congress to restrict outbound U.S. investments that support the military and advanced tech capabilities of foreign adversaries, including the CCP.

26.title: “Now Is the Time for Action”: Moolenaar Demands Ban on Research Ties to Restricted Entities
26.description:
Select Committee Chairman John Moolenaar asks witnesses if U.S. taxpayer dollars should ever support research involving individuals or entities on U.S. government restricted lists.

In this line of questioning, Chairman Moolenaar:
•Secures on-the-record acknowledgments that such collaborations are a “high-risk factor”
•Highlights gaps where agencies still lack clear, written policies
•Commends NSF’s draft policy but urges immediate, government-wide action
•Calls for a consistent federal standard so every research institution knows taxpayer funds cannot flow to restricted entities flagged for national security, export control, sanctions, or human rights concerns

27.title: Dr. Valdez Details NIH Measures to Protect America’s Biomedical Research from Malign Foreign Actors
27.description:
Dr. Patricia Valdez, Chief Extramural Research Integrity Officer at National Institutes of Health (NIH) testifies before the House Select Committee on China.

She outlines NIH’s strengthened research security program to protect taxpayer-funded biomedical research from foreign interference—while preserving legitimate international collaboration. Dr. Valdez details updated disclosure requirements, mandatory research security training, a prohibition on malign foreign talent recruitment programs, and a new “linked foreign subproject” model that increases transparency and financial accountability for foreign collaborations.

28.title: Jeremy Ison: DOE Research Safeguards and the China Tech Threat
28.description:
Mr. Jeremy Ison, Chief of Staff to the Under Secretary for Science at the Department of Energy testifies before the House Select Committee on China.

Ison outlines: 
•DOE’s research security framework across 17 national laboratories
•The China-related threats targeting U.S. science and technology
•Use of a Science & Technology Risk Matrix to flag sensitive but unclassified research
•Enforcement of DOE Order 486.1A on malign foreign talent recruitment programs
•How DOE can condition, mitigate, or deny funding when risks can’t be managed
•The balance between open collaboration and national security protections
•DOE’s role in training the next generation of American STEM and national security talent

29.title: Dr. Keiser Details NSF’s Crackdown on Malign Foreign Talent Programs and CCP Influence
29.description:
Dr. Rebecca Keiser, Chief of Research Security Strategy and Policy and Acting Chief of Staff at the National Science Foundation (NSF), testifies before the House Select Committee on China.

Dr. Keiser explains how NSF is:
•Protecting U.S. taxpayer-funded R&D from malign foreign actors, notably the People’s Republic of China
•Implementing NSPM-33 and Congressionally mandated research security reforms
•Strengthening safeguards on NSF-funded computing resources, including through the NSF Access Program
•Advancing policies to prohibit collaboration with entities on restricted entity lists
•Enforcing bans on malign foreign talent recruitment programs
•Working with federal law enforcement, the intelligence community, and NSF OIG to hold bad actors accountable

30.title: Opening Statement | Chairman Moolenaar on Protecting Federally Funded Research from CCP Exploitation
30.description:
Chairman John Moolenaar opens the House Select on China’s hearing on protecting American taxpayer-funded research from CCP exploitation.
In his opening statement, Chairman Moolenaar:
•Highlights how U.S. leadership in science and technology depends on an open, world‑class research enterprise
•Details how the Chinese Communist Party uses military‑civil fusion and its 2017 National Security Law to turn “civilian” research into military power
•Cites documented cases where Pentagon‑funded stealth research was diverted to support China’s J‑20 fighter

31.title: China’s Missile Threat, Fentanyl Pipeline, and Iran-Russia Ties | Rep. John Moolenaar
31.description:
Select Committee Chairman Rep. John Moolenaar joins Fox News to break down China’s latest JL-3 missile test, its growing nuclear arsenal, and what it means for the Indo-Pacific and the United States.

He also details:
- How Beijing uses military intimidation against Taiwan and U.S. allies like Japan, South Korea, Australia, and the Philippines
- China’s role in fueling the fentanyl crisis through precursor chemicals
- Beijing’s support for Iran and Russia, including energy purchases and dual-use technology like drone parts

32.title: China’s Push to Take Taiwan by 2027: Moolenaar on Fox
32.description:
Select Committee Chairman John Moolenaar joins Fox Business and discusses his Taiwan op-ed and why the U.S. must keep the status quo across the Taiwan Strait as China’s aggression escalates.

He outlines:
-Xi Jinping’s order for the PLA to be ready to take Taiwan by force by 2027
-How a conflict over Taiwan could upend the global economy and cost $10 trillion
-Why European nations and Indo-Pacific partners must join the U.S. in deterring Beijing

Read his op-ed here: https://chinaselectcommittee.house.gov/media/in-the-news/icymi-chairman-moolenaar-writes-keep-the-status-quo-for-taiwan 

Watch the full interview here: https://www.foxbusiness.com/video/6400542370112

33.title: Rep. Moolenaar on Fox: China Is Enabling Iran’s Missile Threat
33.description:
House Select Committee on China Chairman John Moolenaar joins Fox Business and reacts to President Trump declaring the Iran ceasefire “over." He warns about China’s role in enabling Iran and Russia.

Moolenaar details Beijing’s nuclear buildup, its goal of 1,000 warheads by 2030, and the growing missile threat posed by the China–Iran–Russia axis ahead of Xi Jinping’s expected visit to the United States.

Watch the full interview here: https://www.foxbusiness.com/video/6400542370112

34.title: Rep. Moolenaar on CNBC: Chinese Lidar, Nvidia, and the Race to Regulate
34.description:
House Select Committee on China Chairman John Moolenaar joins CNBC to discuss how Congress is responding to the growing threat from the Chinese Communist Party — from economic aggression and IP theft to national security risks and critical supply chains.
Chairman Moolenaar outlines the stakes for American workers and businesses, why CCP influence is a direct threat to U.S. freedom and prosperity, and what Congress is doing to protect our economy, our data, and our allies.

In this conversation, Moolenaar discusses proposed legislation to phase out Chinese-made lidar technology over concerns it could transmit information to the CCP, and his push to ban Chinese vehicles from U.S. roads. He pushes back on assurances from sensor manufacturer Hesai, citing risks tied to connected vehicles and potential back doors in technology — including robots.

Moolenaar also calls for a bipartisan approach to counter the CCP, addresses Nvidia's ambition to put its system in every car, and highlights how legislation continues to lag behind emerging technologies like AI.

Watch the whole segment here: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/07/hesai-technology-nvidia-cyber-risk.html

35.title: On CNBC: Rep. Moolenaar Sounds Alarm on U.S. Drug Trials in China
35.description:
On CNBC’s “Squawk Box,” House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party Chairman John Moolenaar warns about major U.S. pharmaceutical companies conducting clinical drug trials in Communist China.

Moolenaar highlights that some trials have taken place in Xinjiang—where both the Trump and Biden administrations have determined a genocide against Uyghur Muslims is occurring—and in People’s Liberation Army (PLA) medical centers.

He raises serious concerns about:
•Whether U.S. companies are doing real due diligence in China.
•Trials in Xinjiang and PLA hospitals with unclear informed consent.
•American firms potentially profiting from unethical practices.
•Long-term risks of critical medical dependence on China, similar to rare earth minerals.
•The CCP’s ability weaponize sensitive research and medical trial information against the United States.

Moolenaar calls for reforms so that U.S. drug trials protect human rights, patients, and national security—not the interests of the Chinese Communist Party.

Learn more: https://chinaselectcommittee.house.gov/media/letters

36.title: Chairman Moolenaar Honors America's 250th Anniversary
36.description:
Today, and in the days ahead, the Select Committee will be celebrating America's 250th anniversary and the values we hold dear. 

As Chairman Rep. John Moolenaar says, "These rights are from our Creator, not the state, and government exists only with the consent of the governed." 

This is vastly different than the oppression and tyranny of the CCP.

37.title: China’s Economic Espionage and Subnational Influence in the United States
37.description:
The House Select Committee on China held a hearing titled "China’s Economic Espionage and Subnational Influence in the United States" on Thursday, June 25 at 10:30 A.M. in the Cannon House Office Building, Room 390.

The witnesses for the hearing:
- Mr. David Shedd, Former Acting Director of the Defense Intelligence Agency
- Mr. Michael Lucci, Founder & CEO of State Armor
- Mr. John C. Yang, President and Executive Director of Asian Americans Advancing Justice

38.title: Rep. Carlos Gimenez Confronts CCP’s AI Disinformation and Corporate Espionage Risks
38.description:
Rep. Carlos A. Gimenez questions former Acting Director of the Defense Intelligence Agency David Shedd and a former U.S. corporate legal director on the Chinese Communist Party’s strategy to undermine American innovation and exploit U.S. companies operating in China.
Key points: 
•Gimenez warns the CCP is stoking opposition to AI and data centers to slow U.S. progress and win the AI race.
•Shedd testifies every foreign company in China has CCP employees, no real cyber control, and is bound by China’s cybersecurity and National Intelligence Laws.
•Gimenez questions claim that firms don’t cooperate with Chinese authorities and flags their operations in China as a major national security risk.

39.title: Rep. Bilirakis Questions David Shedd on CCP Economic Espionage and CFIUS Blind Spots
39.description:
Rep. Gus M. Bilirakis questions former Acting Director of the Defense Intelligence Agency David Shedd about the Chinese Communist Party’s use of legal acquisitions and economic espionage to obtain sensitive U.S. technology, customer data, and intellectual property.

Shedd warns that the risk from CCP-linked acquisitions remains “very high” and highlights Beijing’s Made in China 2025, now extended to 2030, with a strategic focus on aerospace and biotechnology—areas where the CCP is determined to catch up and surpass the United States.

Rep. Bilirakis also presses Shedd on:
•How the intelligence community assesses CCP efforts to acquire U.S. companies
•How that compares to the risk posed by cyber breaches
•What mechanisms exist—outside CFIUS jurisdiction—to warn policymakers and the private sector about risky deals
•Why the U.S. needs stronger economic and financial intelligence on the CCP to protect national security

40.title: Rep. Johnson Presses Shedd: How Do We Protect U.S. IP from China Without Crushing Business?
40.description:
Former CIA official David Shedd lays out a “small yard, high fences” strategy to protect America’s economic crown jewels from the Chinese Communist Party in questioning from Rep. Dave Johnson.

Shedd explains how the U.S. can:
•Protect critical R&D and IP without turning U.S. companies into arms of the state
•Expose Chinese front companies and investments in U.S. venture capital and private equity
•Elevate security to the C-suite so companies treat core IP as national security infrastructure
•Identify firms tied to Chinese intelligence, security services, or the PLA that should not receive U.S. taxpayer-backed contracts

Rep. Johnson presses Shedd on how to hit the “Goldilocks” balance: defending U.S. innovation from the CCP’s theft and espionage without overregulating American businesses or copying China’s model of state control.

41.title: House Ways and Means Chairman Smith Warns of National Security Threat from CCP-Linked Nonprofits
41.description:
Chairman Jason Smith of the House Ways and Means Committee spoke before the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party about how CCP-linked networks are exploiting America’s tax code to influence our politics, stoke unrest, and undermine U.S. national security.

The Chairman outlines:
•A web of U.S.-based tax-exempt organizations tied to Shanghai-based activist Neville Roy Singham
•Foreign-funded groups allegedly peddling CCP propaganda and interfering in American public discourse
•Efforts by CCP-aligned interests to weaponize nonprofits to protest U.S. data centers and weaken America’s leadership in AI

The Ways and Means Committee, in coordination with the Select Committee on the CCP, is following the money, demanding documents from entities including Breakthrough News, Tricontinental, and The People’s Forum, and is prepared to use subpoena power to protect the integrity of our tax laws and our national security.

42.title: Michael Lucci: How the CCP Is Exploiting U.S. States, Universities, and Critical Bases
42.description:
At a Select Committee on the CCP hearing, State Armor founder and CEO Michael Lucci warns that the American homeland is now contested territory. He details how CCP-linked actors are prepositioning near U.S. military bases—from a former PLA officer buying 140,000 acres by Laughlin Air Force Base, to Huawei equipment around nuclear missile silos in Nebraska, and CCP-tied properties touching the fence lines at Whiteman and Barksdale Air Force Bases.

Lucci calls CCP penetration of American universities a national security crisis, with U.S. taxpayer-funded research flowing into partnerships with Chinese military-linked entities, effectively subsidizing the PLA’s modernization. He highlights bipartisan countermeasures in Nebraska and Texas—foreign agent registration, bans on CCP-linked lobbying funds, transnational repression laws, protections for critical infrastructure, research, and genetic data, and a state cyber command in Texas.

He also details pressure campaigns and cyberattacks targeting state lawmakers, witnesses, and hearings, warning that Beijing is exploiting America’s openness and federalism—and urging urgent action to harden the homeland against CCP influence and subnational prepositioning.

43.title: DIA's David Shedd Details CCP’s Global Campaign to Steal U.S. Technology and Power
43.description:
At a Select Committee on China hearing, former Acting Director of the Defense Intelligence Agency David Shedd exposes the CCP’s massive, decades-long campaign to steal American technology and industrial secrets.

Shedd explains how Beijing uses cyber hacks, human spies, academic partnerships, and weaponized capital to loot U.S. innovation across every sector—AI, telecom, hypersonics, biotech, even agriculture—fueling China’s military buildup and economic rise.

He warns that many U.S. companies are “committing corporate suicide” by ignoring IP theft and chasing short-term profits in China and urges policymakers and business leaders to confront this industrial-scale espionage and the growing risk of conflict over Taiwan.

44.title: Opening Statement | Chairman Moolenaar Exposes Economic Espionage & Malign Influence
44.description:
At today’s hearing, Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China delivers a powerful opening statement addressing China’s United Front strategy aimed at exploiting our local governments, academic institutions, businesses, and Chinese diaspora communities.

Last month, Eileen Wang, the mayor of Arcadia, California, home to 60,000 people, was arrested for acting as an illegal agent of the Chinese government.

The hearing underscores the urgent need for a coordinated nationwide response, including:
•Better intelligence sharing from federal agencies to state and local partners
•Clear guidance for mayors, universities, and community organizations to spot and resist CCP influence
•A whole-of-society strategy to protect our economic competitiveness, safeguard U.S. research, and strengthen the resilience of local communities.

45.title: Chairman Moolenaar Calls for China to Immediately Release Unjustly Detained U.S. Citizen, Min Zin

47.title: Wang Dan’s Story: The Transnational Legacy of Tiananmen Square

48.title: Remembering Tiananmen Square: 37 Years Later
48.description: Join the Select China Committee and Special Guests to commemorate Tiananmen Square, where on this day 37 years ago, tens of thousands of innocent Chinese people dreaming of a better life for their country gathered to seek freedom and democracy.

49.title: Remembering Tiananmen Square: Arthur Liu’s Story
49.description:
Alysa Liu’s gold medal-winning skating captured the hearts of the world at the 2026 Winter Olympics.

Behind the skating lies an amazing backstory: Alysa’s father, Arthur Liu, fled China at the age of 25 in the wake of the 1989 Tiananmen Square Massacre. Arthur was at the Tiananmen Square protests and will join the Select Committee for a bipartisan press conference TOMORROW June 4 at 8:00 AM at the House Triangle.

50.title: Are Chinese Cars Spying on Americans? Chairman Moolenaar Explains on CNBC
50.description:
China is turning “connected” cars into rolling surveillance devices, warns House Select Committee on China Chairman Rep. John Moolenaar in this CNBC interview.

Chairman Moolenaar discusses a new bipartisan bill to ban the import, manufacture, and sale of Chinese autos in the United States, citing:
- National security risks from Chinese-connected vehicles mapping sensitive locations and collecting American data
- Unfair trade practices, including forced labor, deep state subsidies, and ties to the Chinese military
- The threat to the U.S. auto industry, which has long been central to America’s defense industrial base, “the arsenal of democracy”

He also addresses:
- Ongoing TikTok concerns, including the content algorithm, CCP influence, and data security
- How the U.S. should rethink its industrial strategy with like-minded allies instead of relying on China
- The depth of bipartisan support in both the House and Senate for blocking Chinese autos and tightening rules on connected vehicles

51.title: New China Select Report: JPMorgan & Bank of America Helped CCP Military-Linked Firm Raise Billions
51.description:
Chairman John Moolenaar of the Select Committee on China explains how JPMorgan Chase and Bank of America helped Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Ltd. (CATL), a company designated by the Pentagon as a Chinese military company, raise billions of dollars on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.

The Committee’s investigation found:
- JPMorgan and Bank of America underwrote CATL’s IPO just months after its Pentagon designation.
- CATL is linked to forced labor and China’s ongoing genocide of the Uyghurs.
- The banks’ due diligence ignored public evidence of CATL’s military ties and forced labor risk, lending U.S. financial credibility to a company supporting our adversary’s military build-up.
- In a separate deal, Morgan Stanley sponsored the IPO of Zijin Gold-International, whose parent company and subsidiaries are on the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA) Entity List.

Chairman Moolenaar’s message is clear: American banks must not help Chinese military companies raise money or legitimacy. The Select Committee’s report calls for serious policy changes to ensure this never happens again and to protect U.S. national security and the American people.

52.title: Crime, Corruption, and Power: Rise of CCP-linked Scam Networks Targeting Americans
52.description:
The House Select Committee on China will hold a hearing titled Crime, Corruption, and Power: The Rise of CCP-linked Scam Networks Targeting Americans and Threatening U.S. Security. The hearing will be held on Tuesday, May 19 at 10:00 A.M. in HVC 210 in the Capitol Visitors Center.

The witnesses for the hearing will be:

• Mr. Jacob Sims, Visiting Fellow, Asia Center at Harvard University 
• Mr. Jason Tower, Senior Expert, Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime 
• Ms. Erin West, Founder and President, Operation Shamrock 

When: Tuesday, May 19 at 10:00 A.M.

Where: 210 House Visitor Center, U.S. Capitol

53.title: Moolenaar Presses Tech Giants on China-Linked Scam Networks Exploiting Social Media
53.description:
At a hearing of the U.S. House Select Committee on China, Chairman John Moolenaar led follow-up questioning of witnesses on the expanding ecosystem behind China-linked scam centers.

The discussion focused on how social media platforms, messaging apps, telecom infrastructure, and crypto channels are being leveraged to recruit victims, run fraud operations, and launder illicit proceeds at scale.

Witnesses raised concerns that major platforms, including Meta products such as Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp, are still being used by organized scam networks, sometimes despite reported internal knowledge of fraudulent activity. The hearing examined whether current enforcement and moderation systems are sufficient, and whether business incentives are undermining meaningful action against abuse.

Lawmakers pressed for stronger accountability, improved enforcement resources, and potential regulatory reforms to reduce harm while preserving legitimate online communication.

54.title: Rep. Shreve Presses Witnesses on China-Linked Scam Syndicates Exploiting USA and Trafficking Workers
54.description:
In a House Select Committee on China hearing, Congressman Shreve delivers a forceful question period on the growing threat of China-linked scam centers and transnational fraud networks targeting Americans.

Shreve highlights how these operations are not isolated fraud shops, but part of a vast criminal ecosystem involving human trafficking, forced labor, money laundering, cryptocurrency abuse, and weak regulatory environments across multiple countries.

He emphasizes the urgent need for coordinated U.S. action, pointing to legislation like the bipartisan Dismantle Foreign Scam Syndicate Act, which proposes a dedicated interagency task force to track networks, freeze illicit funds faster, support victims, and disrupt scam infrastructure before it moves jurisdictions.

Witnesses also raise concerns about the role of major technology platforms and messaging apps in enabling recruitment, targeting, and laundering activity—alongside crypto firms and stablecoin systems that can be exploited by criminal networks.

The hearing underscores a central warning: these scam operations are not just overseas crimes—they are a direct and growing national security and economic threat to American families.

55.title: Rep. Nathaniel Moran Exposes Industrial-Scale China-Linked Scam Centers Targeting Americans
55.description:
During a House Select Committee on China hearing, Congressman Nathaniel Moran delivered a forceful questioning on the rise of transnational scam networks operating out of Southeast Asia and linked to Chinese organized crime. Moran highlighted staggering losses, at least $10 billion stolen from Americans through cyber fraud, and described a “factory-scale” criminal ecosystem built on human trafficking, forced labor, and sophisticated digital deception.

Witnesses explained how these scam operations differ from traditional fraud due to their global scale, protection by local power structures, and highly organized criminal infrastructure. The discussion also emphasized how everyday Americans are being targeted across all demographics and how victims often don’t realize they are being scammed until it is too late.

The hearing explored how law enforcement, local jurisdictions, and international cooperation can better respond to these evolving threats, including improved training for investigators and stronger cryptocurrency tracing capabilities using Cryptocurrency analysis.

56.title: Rep. LaHood Question Witnesses on China-Linked Scam Networks, $10B Fraud Crisis & Tech-Enabled Crime
56.description:
During this question period before the Select Committee on China hearing, Congressman Darin LaHood highlights the growing threat of transnational scam ecosystems linked to Southeast Asia and China-enabled criminal networks.

LaHood underscores how these fraud operations are stealing billions from American victims, estimated at more than $10 billion annually, and increasingly leveraging cryptocurrency, artificial intelligence, and global digital infrastructure to scale their operations. He raises concerns about how vulnerable populations are targeted, how victims often wait years for compensation, and how government and law enforcement systems are struggling to keep pace.

Witnesses respond by emphasizing the need for stronger interagency coordination, increased funding for law enforcement and diplomatic efforts, and greater accountability from private-sector companies whose platforms, telecommunications infrastructure, and supply chains are being exploited by criminal syndicates.

The discussion also examines the role of social media platforms in enabling scams, as well as the broader ecosystem of global supply chains that support these operations, calling for a comprehensive review of how these networks function and how they can be disrupted.

57.title: Inside the Global Scam Economy: Congress Confronts China-Linked Fraud Networks Targeting Americans
57.description:
In this House Select Committee on China hearing, Chairman John Moolenaar leads a powerful question period examining the rapidly expanding network of China-linked scam compounds operating across Southeast Asia and targeting Americans.

Witnesses including victim advocate Erin West, researcher Jacob Sims, and security analyst Jason Tower detail how these industrial-scale fraud operations function, how victims are left without adequate law enforcement support, and how criminal networks exploit regulatory gaps across borders.

Moolenaar presses witnesses on:
- The failure of local systems to support scam victims once they report fraud
- How scam operators were displaced from China into more permissive jurisdictions
- Links between scam compounds and Chinese state-linked or state-owned entities
- How Beijing’s regional security engagement may be shaping enforcement dynamics in Southeast Asia
- What U.S. strategy is needed to counter transnational scam networks while maintaining effective international cooperation

This hearing highlights growing concerns that these scam centers are not isolated criminal enterprises, but part of a sophisticated, cross-border ecosystem with geopolitical implications.

58.title: Jason Tower: How China-Linked Scam Syndicates Became a Global Security Threat
58.description:
In his opening statement before the Select Committee on China, Jason Tower outlines how China-linked scam syndicates have evolved into a global, industrial-scale criminal ecosystem. He explains how decades of policy decisions, regional instability, and transnational criminal networks contributed to the rise of scam compounds across Southeast Asia and beyond.

Tower details how Chinese domestic crackdowns, including mass prosecutions and sweeping anti-scam campaigns, have displaced criminal operations overseas, where they increasingly target international victims, including Americans. He also highlights links between scam infrastructure, corruption, and entities tied to broader Chinese state-linked initiatives.

The testimony examines key hotspots such as Myanmar, the role of armed groups and governance vacuums, and how scam networks are adapting and dispersing globally. Tower concludes with policy recommendations for the United States, including enhanced intelligence sharing, global coordination mechanisms, and stronger anti-corruption partnerships.

This hearing underscores growing concern that online scam operations are no longer a regional issue, but a global security challenge with strategic implications.

59.title: Harvard Expert Jacob Sims Warns of “Scam State Architecture” Behind China-Linked Fraud Networks
59.description:
At a Select Committee on China hearing, Jacob Sims of the Harvard University Asia Center delivers a stark warning: scam compounds are only the visible front of a much deeper and more dangerous system.

Sims explains how transnational criminal networks, many linked to actors from China, have become embedded within the political and economic structures of countries like Cambodia. He describes this model as “scam state architecture,” a three-layer system involving foreign capital, local oligarch protection, and elite political facilitators.

The result is a powerful and scalable ecosystem enabling cyber scams, human trafficking, and money laundering, impacting victims across the United States and around the world.

Sims urges policymakers to move beyond targeting individual scam compounds and instead confront the broader system:
• Hold system-level enablers accountable
• Support journalists and civil society on the front lines
• Build coordinated international strategies to prevent expansion

This testimony highlights the growing national security threat posed by state-enabled cybercrime networks—and what must be done to stop them.

60.title: Operation Shamrock's Erin West Exposes China-Linked “Scamdemic” Draining Americans’ Life Savings
60.description:
At a Select Committee on China hearing, Operation Shamrock’s Erin West delivers a powerful opening statement on the rise of China-linked scam centers targeting Americans.

Through real stories—like a U.S. Army veteran who lost 90% of his retirement, a Florida engineer forced to track down criminals overseas, and a Wisconsin paralegal who built her own case—West highlights the devastating human toll of what she calls a global “scamdemic.”

Her testimony reveals how transnational criminal networks operate scam compounds across Southeast Asia, often with local protection, while exploiting gaps in U.S. law enforcement capacity and accountability from technology platforms.

West warns that this is no longer just fraud, it is a growing national security threat tied to illicit finance, human trafficking, and regional instability.

61.title: Opening Statement | Chairman Moolenaar Exposes China-Linked Scam Centers Stealing Billions from USA
61.description:
At today’s hearing, Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China delivers a powerful opening statement on the growing threat of China-linked scam centers.

In 2024 alone, Americans lost at least $10 billion to sophisticated fraud networks operating across Southeast Asia. These aren’t isolated scams—they are part of a massive ecosystem involving cybercrime, human trafficking, and illicit finance.

The Committee’s new investigative report reveals:
- How China-linked criminal networks operate at industrial scale
- The role of weak governance and corruption in enabling scam compounds
- Evidence that a Chinese state-owned company directly contracted to build scam centers
- The use of forced labor and human trafficking inside these operations
- How these networks undermine U.S. national security and regional stability

Chairman Moolenaar makes clear: the Chinese government has the ability to act but has chosen not to.

The hearing also highlights ongoing U.S. efforts to crack down on these networks and calls for urgent congressional action, including passage of the Dismantle Foreign Scam Syndicates Act.

62.title: China’s Economic Espionage and Subnational Influence in the United States
62.description:
Witnesses:
Mr. David Shedd, Former Acting Director of the Defense Intelligence Agency
Mr. Michael Lucci, Founder & CEO of State Armor

63.title: Trump’s China Trip, Xi’s Taiwan Threat, and Iran-Russia Axis: Chairman Moolenaar with Trey Gowdy
63.description:
House Select Committee on China Chairman John Moolenaar joins Trey Gowdy on Sunday Night in America to break down:

- President Trump’s recent visit to China and the invitation for Xi Jinping to visit the U.S.
- How Beijing is backing Iran and Russia while claiming to support stability in the Middle East
- The growing threats against Taiwan, and why U.S. arms sales and deterrence are critical
- China’s role in the fentanyl crisis and the fight to free prisoners of conscience like Jimmy Lai and Pastor Jen
- Why the U.S. must protect its technology, supply chains, and intellectual property from abuse by the Chinese Communist Party

Chairman Moolenaar explains why Congress formed the House Select Committee on China, how the CCP has grown more authoritarian and aggressive under Xi, and what the U.S. must do with allies to deter conflict and defend American security.

64.title: Inside the Trump–Xi Meeting: Chairman Moolenaar on What’s Really at Risk
64.description:
Chairman of the House Select Committee on China, John Moolenaar, joins NBC’s Kristen Welker to break down President Trump’s high-stakes meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Moolenaar discusses the delicate balance between diplomacy and competition with China, rising tensions over Taiwan, and the Chinese Communist Party’s global influence.

The conversation also dives into new reports of China potentially supplying weapons to Iran, Beijing’s role in global energy markets, and its economic ties to Russia and Iran. Moolenaar outlines U.S. priorities, including protecting American workers, securing critical supply chains, and countering China’s involvement in fentanyl trafficking.

65.title: Chinese EVs Are ‘Rolling Data Collection Devices’ | Chairman Moolenaar with 535's Marianna Sotomayor
65.description:
Chairman John Moolenaar warns that Chinese-made EVs are “rolling data collection devices” and a growing threat to U.S. national security. From cars and drones to cranes in our ports, China is using connected tech to gather data on America.

In this interview on “535” with Marianna Sotomayor, Moolenaar, Chairman of the Select Committee on China, discusses:

- His bipartisan bill with Rep. Debbie Dingell to restrict Chinese EVs and sensitive components
- How Chinese tech (EVs, DJI drones, internet-connected cranes, batteries) can “phone home” to the CCP
- The impact of unfair Chinese trade practices on U.S. auto jobs, manufacturing, and our military industrial base
- Concerns about Chinese EVs entering via Canada and what that means for border states like Michigan
- Gas prices, Iran, and why he says EV adoption should be driven by consumer choice, not federal mandates
- The Committee’s work to expose CCP-enabled scam centers stealing billions from Americans
- Why he believes the China Select Committee must remain and continue its bipartisan work

66.title: Moolenaar: CCP Is Stealing U.S. Tech and Cheating American Workers
66.description:
Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China joins FOX News to respond to President Xi’s summit remarks that the U.S. and China should be “partners, not rivals.”

Chairman Moolenaar discusses:
- How the CCP is undermining U.S. efforts with Iran and Russia
- Technology theft and how China is cheating American workers
- The need for concrete action from Beijing on fentanyl
- U.S. resolve on Taiwan and the CCP’s propaganda spin
- Why America must pursue peace through strength and a fair trade relationship

Stay updated on the work of the House Select Committee on China and its efforts to protect American workers, national security, and our allies.

67.title: $10,000 for Insider Information: How the CCP Tried to Buy Access to the House China Committee
67.description:
Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China joins NTD to respond to the stunning case of Mayor Eileen Wong, a former Arcadia, California official who pleaded guilty to acting as a foreign agent for Beijing.

In this interview, Chairman Moolenaar explains:
- How the CCP’s “united front” operations target Chinese American communities and Chinese nationals in the United States
- The use of front groups, cultural associations, and media outlets—including Wong’s “US News Center” website—as tools for Beijing’s propaganda
- A CCP-linked offer of $10,000 to a Select Committee staffer for inside information on U.S. policy and committee work
- Why the CCP’s information warfare seeks to discredit democracy, silence dissent, and export repression beyond China’s borders
- The stakes for fair trade, technology security, and U.S. national security as President Trump travels to Beijing to meet Xi Jinping
- Why President Trump must raise prisoners of conscience, religious freedom, and basic human dignity, echoing President Reagan’s advocacy for people behind the Iron Curtain

👉 Subscribe for more updates from the House Select Committee on the CCP on U.S.–China relations, national security, technology, and human rights.

68.title: Chairman Moolenaar: President Xi Must Free Jimmy Lai — U.S. Will Defend Taiwan & Lead in AI
68.description:
House Select Committee on China Chairman John Moolenaar (R-MI) joins NewsNation to react to President Trump’s high-stakes trip to China and his meeting with Xi Jinping.

Moolenaar says the U.S.–China relationship must be grounded in American national security, human dignity, and economic strength, and that President Trump is entering talks with Xi from a position of strength.

69.title: Today, we honor these women, and all mothers who refuse to back down in the face of injustice.
69.description:
This Mother’s Day, we honor not only the love and sacrifice of mothers, but the extraordinary courage of those who stand up to the tyranny of the CCP.
 
We remember the unwavering resolve of Ding Zilin and Zhang Xianling, who have spent decades demanding accountability for the lives lost at Tiananmen Square.
 
We recognize the strength of Nurungul Tohti and Gulshan Abbas, whose families have been torn apart by China's systemic oppression of Uyghur communities.
 
We stand with Pu Wenqing, Shao Wenxia, Keke the mother of Niu Tengyu, He Fangmei, and Yin Min, mothers who have faced surveillance, detention, and intimidation simply for protecting their children and speaking out.
 
Today, we honor these women, and all mothers who refuse to back down in the face of injustice. Their courage inspires the world.

70.title: Moolenaar: We Must Stop China from Buying U.S. Farmland & Our Best AI Chips
70.description:
House Select Committee on China Chairman John Moolenaar joins Maria Bartiromo on FOX News to discuss China’s role in enabling Iran, Beijing’s push to buy American farmland, and the race for leadership in artificial intelligence.

Chairman Moolenaar warns that China is:
- Buying up to 90% of Iran’s oil and supplying parts for Iranian military equipment
- Using satellites and advanced tech to support Iran’s targeting and tracking
- Trying to access America’s best AI chips for dual-use military applications
- Increasing its stake in U.S. farmland, including land near sensitive military sites

Moolenaar outlines a new bill to:
- Block Chinese Communist Party–linked entities from buying U.S. farmland and land near military bases
- Strengthen federal review of foreign land purchases around critical infrastructure and energy facilities
- Ensure the Agriculture Secretary has a formal role in reviewing these high-risk transactions

He also weighs in on:
- The President’s upcoming meeting with Xi Jinping
- How the U.S. can maintain its lead in AI while tightening export controls on advanced chips
- Why food security is national security in the competition with the Chinese Communist Party

👉 Subscribe for more conversations with members of the House Select Committee on China about U.S.-China competition, national security, and protecting American workers and families.

71.title: Chairman John Moolenaar on Blocking China’s Chip Access and Winning the AI Race
71.description:
House Select Committee on China Chairman John Moolenaar joins Maria Bartiromo on FOX News to discuss the Commerce Department’s move to restrict semiconductor equipment exports to China’s Hua Hong Semiconductor.

Chairman Moolenaar explains why limiting China’s access to advanced chip technology is critical to protecting U.S. national security and maintaining America’s lead in artificial intelligence. He outlines the risks of enabling China’s military capabilities through advanced computing and calls for a “rolling technical threshold” to ensure the U.S. continues to outpace Beijing.

Chairman Moolenaar emphasizes that the U.S. must lead in AI development, safeguard critical technologies, and ensure American innovation is not leveraged against U.S. interests.

72.title: Common Ground on China: Rep. John Moolenaar and Rep. Ro Khanna Warn About Rare Earths and Iran
72.description:
In this Common Ground segment, Chairman John Moolenaar and Ranking Member Ro Khanna of the House Select Committee on China sit down to discuss how the United States should respond to the growing challenge from the CCP.

They cover:
- China’s support for Iran, Russia, and North Korea – including buying an estimated 90% of Iran’s oil
- The Strait of Hormuz, global energy security, and China’s reaction to U.S. actions in the region
- China’s monopoly on rare earths and critical minerals essential for phones, advanced technology, and U.S. military applications
- U.S. dependence on Chinese pharmaceutical ingredients and the need for secure supply chains
- The technology race with China, economic security, and human rights concerns inside the PRC
- How Republicans and Democrats on the Committee are finding bipartisan common ground to protect America’s national interest

Despite policy differences, both members emphasize respectful debate, cross-party cooperation, and putting Team America first.

73.title: China’s Campaign to Steal America’s AI Edge - Part II
73.description:
Witnesses:
Mr. Dmitri Alperovitch, Chairman, Silverado Policy Accelerator
Mr. Yusuf Mahmood, Director of AI and Emerging Technology, America First Policy Institute

75.title: April 16, 2026
75.description:
Chairman @repmoolenaar joined @MariaBartiromo today to outline China's multi-front strategy: finance, technology transfer, and influence operations, all reinforcing one another.

China continues to buy Iran's oil, enable sanctions evasion for the regimes in Moscow and Tehran, and expand its influence operations in the U.S.

76.title: Does winning mean developing the world's most powerful AI models?
76.description:
America has the edge in the world’s most powerful AI models, no question. But China is playing a different game: efficiency, scale, and global deployment.

Kyle Chan from @BrookingsInstitution explains:
"Does winning mean developing the world's most powerful AI models? If yes, then the us has the decisive lead. American ai models are widely recognized as the best in the world on virtually every metric you can think of, from math and reasoning to coding and AI agents, American private companies continue to set the pace at the technological frontier supported by deep capital markets, a dynamic innovation ecosystem, and the best talent from around the world. China's AI models are improving quickly but continue to lag behind. Chinese AI companies face real constraints on compute due to our export controls and their own limited capital resources, so instead they're prioritizing other goals. They're focused on efficiency, building models that are cheaper to train and run. They're focused on adoption using an open source strategy to win users around the world, and they're focused on integration with other platforms and services. On sheer performance, I would expect the gap between our models and theirs to persist or even widen over time. But model performance is not everything."

77.title: Moolenaar Sounds Alarm on China-Iran Ties, Fentanyl, and U.S. Vulnerabilities
77.description:
In this interview, FOX News' Maria Bartiromo speaks with House China Select Committee Chairman John Moolenaar about rising concerns over China’s global influence and its ties to Iran.

The discussion follows remarks from President Donald Trump regarding a recent exchange of letters with Xi Jinping, as well as new reports about Chinese support for Iran’s economy and potential military capabilities.

Moolenaar also highlights how economic and geopolitical strategies, ranging from energy policy to sanctions, are shaping the U.S. position ahead of future engagements with Beijing.

78.title: Rep. Young Kim Presses Witnesses on China, Supply Chains, and U.S. National Security Risks
78.description: Congresswoman Young Kim leads a focused question period with expert witnesses on critical issues shaping America’s national security and economic future. Lawmakers press for answers on U.S. competitiveness, global supply chains, and the strategic challenges posed by China’s rise.

79.title: Rep. Gus Bilirakis Presses Experts on Semiconductor Security, Taiwan Risk & AI Trade Barriers
79.description:
During a key question period led by Rep. Gus Bilirakis, he presses expert witnesses on the fragility of the global semiconductor supply chain and its implications for U.S. economic and national security.

A witness highlighted a sobering estimate that a disruption to Taiwan’s semiconductor production could reduce U.S. economic output by up to 11%, a shock greater than the 2008 recession. The discussion underscored the importance of scaling domestic chip production, including advanced and foundational semiconductors, and strengthening cooperation with allies such as Japan and South Korea.

Experts pointed to ongoing efforts like the CHIPS Act and major new fabrication investments in the United States as critical steps toward resilience, while warning that China continues to pursue dominance in foundational chip manufacturing.

Overall, the exchange highlighted growing bipartisan concern over semiconductor dependency, AI competition, and the future of U.S. technological leadership.

80.title: Chairman Moolenaar Questions Witnesses On China AI Race, Export Controls & Model Distillation Risks
80.description:
In this question period, Chairman John Moolenaar presses leading experts on the strategic competition with China in artificial intelligence, focusing on whether the U.S. can or should use advanced semiconductor exports to shape China’s dependence on the American AI stack.

Dmitri Alperovitch argues that chips alone do not constitute the full U.S. AI ecosystem and warns that selling advanced semiconductors to China does not meaningfully create long-term technological dependence. He highlights that modern AI systems rely on diverse compute infrastructure across multiple vendors, and that switching costs between chip architectures are lower than often assumed.

Kyle Chan discusses the dual effects of export controls, slowing China’s AI progress in the short term while incentivizing long-term domestic semiconductor development that could reduce U.S. leverage over time. He emphasizes the need for a broader, more comprehensive policy approach beyond export restrictions alone.

Yusuf Mahmood addresses adversarial model distillation, where foreign actors may extract capabilities from U.S. AI systems in ways that may not violate existing law. He outlines potential federal responses, including enhanced intelligence monitoring, interagency coordination, voluntary industry standards, and improved information-sharing mechanisms to counter these emerging threats.

81.title: "It all comes down to compute."

82.title: The CCP is pursuing AI dominance by 2030. And when it cannot compete fairly, it steals.
82.description:
The CCP is pursuing AI dominance by 2030. And when it cannot compete fairly, it steals.

Yusuf Mahmood from @a1policy explains: 
"We are not prepared to secure our AI systems. If we decided tomorrow that it was a top national security priority to prevent the CCP from stealing our most capable AI software, we would face extraordinary challenges. We're starting from a vulnerable position. The CCP seeks full AI domination by 2030, and it lacks the capital and talent to win fairly, so it steals. These aren't theoretical harms right now. Chinese AI, developed from stolen American technology, is helping Iran target American warfighters."

83.title: What Does “Winning” the AI Race Actually Mean? | Kyle Chan Testifies
83.description:
Kyle Chan of the Brookings Institution delivers compelling testimony on what it truly means for the United States to “win” in the AI race with China.

While the U.S. leads in frontier models and innovation, Chan warns that China is rapidly advancing in efficiency, deployment, and energy capacity, raising urgent questions about long-term competitiveness.

He emphasizes that winning in AI isn’t just about technological dominance, it’s about translating that leadership into prosperity, resilience, and security for the American people.

84.title: CCP Stealing U.S. AI Technology? Yusuf Mahmood Sounds Alarm in Congress
84.description:
Yusuf Mahmood, Director of AI and Emerging Technology Policy at the America First Policy Institute, delivers a stark warning to Congress: the United States is not prepared to defend its most advanced artificial intelligence systems from exploitation by the Chinese Communist Party (CCP).

In this opening statement, Mahmood outlines how adversaries are targeting U.S. AI through:

- Industrial-scale distillation attacks to replicate American models
- Trade secret theft, including insider threats
- Vulnerabilities in model weight security
- Emerging risks like data poisoning that can implant hidden backdoors

He also details the real-world consequences, warning that stolen or compromised AI technology is already being used in ways that could endanger American warfighters.

85.title: Dmitri Alperovitch Warns: AI Race Will Decide the 21st Century
85.description:
Cybersecurity expert Dmitri Alperovitch delivers a stark warning to Congress: the global race for artificial intelligence supremacy is already underway, and the outcome could define the 21st century.

Testifying before the Select Committee on China, Alperovitch explains why compute power, not talent, data, or funding, is the decisive factor in AI leadership. At the center of this competition are advanced semiconductor chips, which are rapidly becoming the most strategic resource in the world.

He outlines how China is aggressively pursuing U.S. AI technology through both legal and illicit channels, including alleged smuggling of advanced chips, and warns of a looming “recursive self-improvement” threshold that could give one nation an irreversible advantage.

86.title: Chairman Moolenaar: China Is Stealing America’s AI Edge Through Chip Smuggling
86.description:
Chairman John Moolenaar delivers his opening statement at a Select Committee on China hearing examining China’s theft of advanced U.S. AI technology.

In his remarks, Chairman Moolenaar outlines how Chinese actors are exploiting legal loopholes, evading export controls, and engaging in large-scale chip smuggling operations—including a $2.5 billion scheme involving altered serial numbers and fake servers—to obtain cutting-edge American semiconductors.

The Chairman also details how China remains dependent on U.S. and allied technology across the AI stack—from semiconductor manufacturing equipment to advanced AI models—and is increasingly turning to theft, including unauthorized model distillation, to close the gap.

As AI reshapes global economic and military power, this hearing underscores the urgent need for Congress to act to protect U.S. technological leadership and prevent Beijing from weaponizing American innovation.

87.title: China isn’t just competing with the U.S.; it’s enabling global instability.
87.description:
China isn’t just competing with the U.S.; it’s enabling global instability.

Chairman Moolenaar, highlighting investigative work from the Select Committee on China, explains how Beijing is buying sanctioned oil from Russia, Iran, and Venezuela through the use of a “shadow fleet” of thousands of ships, and in exchange supplies dual-use technology that fuels Iran and Russia's war efforts.

88.title: Christians in China face persecution, state regulation, and forced Sinicization.
88.description:
Over the next several days, Christians in the United States and around the world will gather at church and within their religious communities to commemorate Holy Thursday, reflect on Good Friday, and celebrate Easter. 

Meanwhile, Christians in China face persecution, state regulation, and forced Sinicization. Pastor Jin's story highlights the ongoing struggle of Christians in China fighting for basic religious freedoms.

The Chinese Communist Party must release Pastor Jin and all individuals persecuted for exercising their religious freedom under authoritarian rule.

89.title: Confront a serious national security challenge: the illicit diversion of advanced U.S. AI chips.
89.description:
As the sponsor of the #ChipSecurityAct, @billhuizenga  is leading efforts to confront a serious national security challenge: the illicit diversion of advanced U.S. AI chips. 

Evidence from enforcement actions, and congressional hearings, show that U.S. technology is being funneled to China. The Chip Security Act strengthens protections, scales effective security practices, and ensures industry can safeguard innovation without disruption. 

Chairman @repmoolenaar in his support of this legislation has made it clear: the U.S. must act now to secure its technological edge and prevent adversaries from accessing the tools that power next-generation military and economic capabilities. 🇺🇸

90.title: Rep. Young Kim: Stand with Japan, Push Back on China
90.description:
The U.S.-Japan alliance is a cornerstone of peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific, and it must be defended.

@ChinaSelect member @RepYoungKim spoke in strong support of H.Res. 971, condemning the Chinese Communist Party’s coercive actions against Japan and reaffirming the United States’ commitment to its allies.

As Rep. Kim emphasized, Beijing’s military intimidation, economic pressure, and threats against Japan are not the actions of a responsible global power; they are attempts to undermine sovereignty and destabilize the region.

Chairman @repmoolenaar  is a proud co-sponsor of this resolution, reinforcing Congress’ unified message: the United States stands with Japan and will push back against CCP coercion.

91.title: Moolenaar: U.S. Must Adopt “Defense Mentality” to Win the AI Race vs China
91.description:
At the Hill & Valley Forum, Chairman Moolenaar captured the core challenge of the AI era:

The U.S. thrives on free markets, innovation, and open trade with trusted partners.

But when facing a strategic competitor that disregards those rules, a different approach is required. As Chairman Moolenaar noted, this moment calls for a more “defense-oriented” mindset, using every available tool to ensure the U.S. prevails.

This is about adapting our strengths to a new reality.

92.title: Innovation is America’s edge—but it’s not enough on its own.
92.description:
Innovation is America’s edge—but it’s not enough on its own.

At Hill & Valley, John Moolenaar warned that competing with China requires a “defense mentality.”

That means strong export controls, secure supply chains, and putting America first.

93.title: The AI race is here—and the stakes couldn’t be higher.
93.description:
The AI race is here—and the stakes couldn’t be higher.

At the Hill & Valley Forum, John Moolenaar made it clear: the U.S. must use every tool available to win.

We can’t let our own technology be used to undermine us. 🇺🇸

94.title: Do you know where your medicine comes from?
94.description:
Do you know where your medicine comes from?

Generic drugs make up nearly 90% of U.S. prescriptions, but the ingredients behind many of them are now largely made overseas, mostly in China.

In fact, 83 of the top 100 generic drugs Americans rely on have no domestic source for key ingredients.

America’s health, and national security, depend on secure supply chains.

More on our recent Select Committee on China hearing, "“From the Science Lab to the Medicine Cabinet: How China is Cornering the Market on Our Medicines," here: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLWhHZxDXQtUWKslws-7aA3I3_ZLYVyFY4

95.title: Chairman John Moolenaar on Winning the AI Race vs China | Hill & Valley Forum 2026
95.description:
At the 2026 Hill & Valley Forum, John Moolenaar, Chairman of the Select Committee on China, joins a high-stakes discussion on how the United States can compete—and win—in the global AI race.

Featuring leaders from government and industry, including Brad Lightcap and Josh Gottheimer, this conversation dives into the strategies shaping the future of artificial intelligence, national security, and economic power.

Chairman Moolenaar outlines why strong enforcement, allied coordination, and American innovation are critical to maintaining leadership—and what’s at stake if the U.S. falls behind.

💡 What does success look like in 10 years? A world where American-led AI drives economic growth, scientific breakthroughs, and safeguards democratic values.

Watch the full conversation to understand the policies, challenges, and opportunities shaping the AI era.

96.title: The growing threat of CCP influence at the UN.
96.description:
At today’s House Appropriations Committee hearing, Chairman Moolenaar and US Representative to the UN Michael Waltz highlighted the growing threat of CCP influence at the UN. 

Our latest investigative report shows how China uses funding, key UN positions, peacekeeping, and proxy NGOs to advance its agenda.

The U.S. is responding by placing Americans in leadership roles, defending transparency, and ensuring the UN serves global peace and security, not authoritarian interests

97.title: PRESS CONFERENCE | Daughters of Political Prisoners Speak Out on CCP Persecution
97.description:
At a powerful press conference, daughters of imprisoned activists exposed the Chinese Communist Party’s ongoing crackdown on religious freedom and pro-democracy voices.

Grace Drexel shared the story of her father, Pastor Ezra Jin, detained for his faith and ministry, while Claire Lai detailed the harsh imprisonment of her father, Hong Kong publisher Jimmy Lai.

Speakers highlighted:

The detention of religious leaders and “prisoners of conscience” in China

Allegations of torture, isolation, and denial of medical care

Calls for U.S. action, including sanctions and diplomatic pressure

The broader pattern of transnational repression targeting families abroad

Chairman John Moolenaar emphasized the need to confront systemic human rights abuses and defend fundamental freedoms.

Reporters in the room include:
Michael Martina - Reuters
Didi Tang - Associated Press
Kamden Mulder - National Review
Eva Fu - The Epoch Times
George Caldwell - The Daily Signal

98.title: China controls the ingredients for 90% of U.S. prescription drugs.
98.description: 90% of U.S. prescriptions rely on ingredients dominated by China. What was once trusted medicine is now a national security risk.

99.title: From the Science Lab to the Medicine Cabinet: How China is Cornering the Market on Our Medicines
99.description:
• Dr. Jacob Becraft, CEO and Co-Founder, Strand Therapeutics Inc. 
• Mr. Patrick Cashman, President, USAntibiotics 
• Dr. Francisco Gimenez, Partner, 8VC 
• Dr. Marta E. Wosińska, Senior Fellow – Economic Studies, Center on Health Policy at Brookings

100.title: Rep. Gus Bilirakis on Securing American Medicine: Countering China & Strengthening Domestic Pharma
100.description:
In this critical congressional hearing, Rep. Gus Bilirakis (R-FL) emphasizes the importance of protecting the U.S. pharmaceutical supply chain from foreign influence and boosting domestic manufacturing. He highlights the launch of the American Made Medicines Caucus and outlines strategies to ensure safe, affordable, and innovative medicines for American patients.

Experts testify on ways to streamline FDA approvals, improve first-in-human trials, and expand domestic bio-manufacturing, creating a stronger, more resilient pharmaceutical ecosystem.

Watch to hear how Congress is working to keep life-saving innovation in the U.S. and ensure patients have access to safe, effective medicines.

101.title: Rep. Zach Nunn Warns: U.S. Must Protect Biotech & Drug Innovation from China
101.description:
In this Congressional question period, Rep. Zach Nunn (R-IA) addresses the growing risks of U.S. dependence on China for critical generic medicines and biotech infrastructure. Drawing on his decades of counterintelligence experience, he highlights how China’s dominance in semiconductors, critical minerals, and early-stage clinical trials threatens both national security and American patients.

Rep. Nunn emphasizes the importance of keeping drug innovation, clinical trials, and life-saving research in the U.S., protecting communities across Iowa and nationwide. He also details the economic benefits of domestic biotech investment and the urgent need to prevent early-stage clinical development from moving overseas.

102.title: Rep. Nathaniel Moran: “China’s Biotech Surge Threatens U.S. Pharmaceutical Leadership”
102.description:
In this congressional question period, Rep. Nathaniel Moran (R-TX) highlights the growing threat China poses to U.S. leadership in biotechnology and pharmaceuticals. With China rapidly expanding clinical trials and dominating the production of key drug ingredients, Rep. Moran stresses the need for America to accelerate innovation, streamline FDA processes, and maintain ethical standards in medical research.

📌 Watch to hear Rep. Moran’s urgent call for U.S. action to preserve leadership in life-saving medicines and ensure safety for American patients.

103.title: Rep. Ashley Hinson Questions Experts on U.S. Drug Supply Security & Biotech Competition with China
103.description:
In this critical congressional question period, Rep. Ashley Hinson (R-IA) highlights the urgent need to protect America’s pharmaceutical supply chain and strengthen domestic biotech innovation. She questions experts on how public and private sectors can collaborate to:

Rep. Hinson emphasizes that U.S. leadership in biotech isn’t just about innovation—it’s about public health, economic stability, and keeping patients out of hospitals. Watch as she explores solutions for a more resilient and competitive pharmaceutical ecosystem.

104.title: Rep. Darin LaHood Questions Witnesses on China’s Threat to U.S. Drug Innovation
104.description:
In this critical congressional hearing, Rep. Darin LaHood (R-IL) highlights the strategic competition between the U.S. and China in biotechnology and pharmaceuticals. From his personal welcome to Dr. Jake Becraft of Metamora, Illinois, to addressing the challenges of clinical trials in the U.S., Rep. LaHood underscores the need to protect American innovation, expand patient access, and safeguard national security.

Watch as Rep. LaHood and Dr. Becraft explore ways to ensure life-saving medicines reach patients faster while keeping innovation domestic.

105.title: Rep. Dan Newhouse Questions Experts on Amoxicillin Shortages & China Biotech Risks
105.description:
In this critical congressional question period, Rep. Dan Newhouse (R-WA) dives into two pressing issues affecting American health and national security: the amoxicillin shortages of 2022–2023 and the risks posed by U.S. investments in Chinese biotechnology.

Experts testify on the challenges of domestic drug manufacturing, pricing mechanisms, and strategies the federal government could implement to prevent future shortages. They also reveal why American firms are cautious about partnering with Chinese biotech, highlighting IP concerns and the need for on-the-ground diligence.

Watch as Rep. Newhouse pushes for solutions to strengthen the U.S. pharmaceutical supply chain and safeguard innovation.

106.title: China Controls Our Medicine: Rep. Neal Dunn Sounds the Alarm on Pharma Supply Chains
106.description:
In a powerful congressional Q&A, Rep. Neal Dunn draws on 35 years as a physician to warn that America’s pharmaceutical supply chains are dangerously dependent on China. Highlighting that nearly 90% of generic drugs—including antibiotics and blood thinners—rely on Chinese manufacturing, Dunn warns this isn’t just a trade issue—it’s a national security and medical readiness crisis.

He explains how China is strategically moving up the pharmaceutical value chain, dominating clinical trials, licensing deals, and essential drug production, potentially putting American lives at risk in a crisis. The discussion also covers the role of tariffs, India’s supply chain, and urgent steps Congress could take to strengthen domestic drug manufacturing.

107.title: Moolenaar Questions Witnesses | Urgent Warning: U.S. Biotech at Risk as China Dominates Drug Trials
107.description:
