Chairman John Moolenaar questions biotech leaders on a startling trend: China now controls nearly half of all major global pharmaceutical licensing deals. Experts warn that the U.S. could lose its edge in early-stage drug development if clinical trials and investor capital continue shifting overseas.

📌 Why it matters: This isn’t just a biotech issue — it’s a national security and economic threat. Every step we take now will determine whether the U.S. remains a global leader in life-saving medicines.

108.title: Dr. Marta Wosinka Testifies | Shocking Truth About America’s Dependence on Chinese Drug Ingredients
108.description:
Dr. Marta Austin Wosinska of the Brookings Institution delivers a stark warning to Congress about the fragility of U.S. generic drug supply chains. With 80% of active ingredients made outside the U.S. and heavy reliance on Chinese chemical inputs, our access to everyday and emergency medications is at risk.

In this testimony, she breaks down four critical questions policymakers must answer to truly de-risk America’s drug supply:

Dr. Woskinska emphasizes the need for smart onshoring, friend-shoring, and targeted investment in critical generics—from hospital antibiotics to widely used medicines—while highlighting the risks of over-reliance on cheap Chinese inputs.

109.title: USAntibiotics's Patrick Cashman | China Controls America’s Antibiotics: A National Security Threat
109.description:
Patrick Cashman, President of USAntibiotics, delivers a sobering warning to Congress about the fragility of the U.S. pharmaceutical supply chain. Once fully made in America, amoxicillin—the nation’s most prescribed antibiotic—now relies heavily on foreign ingredients, with China dominating key supply layers. Cashman explains how decades of subsidized foreign competition, lax oversight, and supply chain opacity have created serious national security risks, including higher adverse event rates for imported generics.

In this testimony, he outlines concrete steps Congress can take to restore domestic drug manufacturing, protect public health, and ensure America can produce critical medicines independently.

110.title: 8VC's Dr. Francisco Gimenez | China’s Biotech Strategy Threatening America’s Innovation Engine
110.description:
8VC partner Dr. Francisco Jimenez warns that China has already begun disrupting America’s biotech industry—and the consequences could be severe for both economic and national security.

Over the past 50 years, the American biotech ecosystem—sparked by pioneers like Genentech—has driven breakthroughs that transformed global medicine. The U.S. bioscience industry now generates $3.2 trillion in economic output, supports 10 million American jobs, and has helped deliver dramatic improvements in survival rates for diseases like HIV, breast cancer, and heart disease.

But according to Dr. Jimenez, China has spent years studying this system and building a state-backed strategy to compete.

Dr. Jimenez argues the stakes go beyond economics. If the U.S. loses its biotech edge, America could also lose the ability to rapidly develop medical countermeasures during future pandemics—similar to the rapid vaccine development seen during COVID-19.

111.title: Dr. Jacob Becraft Testifies | China Is Beating the U.S. in Biotech— It’s a National Security Threat
111.description:
Is the United States falling behind in the race for the future of medicine?

Strand Therapeutics CEO Dr. Jacob Becraft warns that China is rapidly overtaking the U.S. in biotechnology, and the consequences go far beyond healthcare.

Dr. Becraft explains how China’s faster, cheaper clinical trial system is drawing innovation overseas, creating a dangerous “flywheel effect” where early human data, investment, and manufacturing all follow. Meanwhile, American biotech companies face regulatory delays, fragmented infrastructure, and rising costs—putting U.S. leadership at risk.

Biotechnology isn’t just about innovation—it’s about economic power, public health, and global leadership. If current trends continue, the center of gravity for life-saving medicines could shift overseas.

112.title: Chairman Moolenaar: China Is Cornering the Market on Our Medicines
112.description:
At today’s Select Committee on China hearing, Chairman John Moolenaar delivered a stark warning about the future of America’s pharmaceutical supply chain—and the growing role of China in both everyday medicines and next-generation drug development.

Roughly 90% of prescriptions filled in the United States are generic drugs, many of which rely on Chinese-controlled inputs. Chairman Moolenaar outlined how decades of state-backed policies have allowed China to dominate key pharmaceutical supply chains—while rapidly expanding into advanced biotech and clinical trials.

He also raised serious concerns about the migration of drug development to China, including ethical risks tied to clinical trials and the long-term impact on U.S. innovation, national security, and public health.

113.title: President Trump revealed Maduro’s fortress was guarded by Russian and Chinese military technology.
113.description:
President Trump revealed Maduro’s fortress was guarded by Russian and Chinese military technology.

Let that sink in.

The Chinese Communist Party isn’t just repressing its own people; it’s exporting authoritarian power to prop up dictators across the globe.

The CCP doesn’t stand for freedom. It stands with tyrants.

114.title: “No nation should ever doubt America’s resolve.”
114.description:
“No nation should ever doubt America’s resolve.”

Tonight, President Trump underscored a clear reality: Iran is advancing missile capabilities that threaten U.S. forces, our allies, and potentially the American homeland.

The Chinese Communist Party continues to enable Iran, which fuels instability, and undermines national security.

Peace Through Strength is essential to deterrence.

115.title: How the SECURE Minerals Act Counters China’s Grip on Critical Minerals | Rep. Rob Wittman Testifies
115.description:
Rep. Rob Wittman, member of the Select Committee on China, delivers testimony before the House Committee on Natural Resources' Subcommittee on Energy and Mineral Resources on his SECURE Minerals Act which is legislation designed to rebuild America’s critical mineral supply chains and counter China’s global dominance.

Critical minerals are essential to the U.S. economy and national defense, powering everything from smartphones and laptops to radar systems and submarines. Today, China controls roughly:

70% of rare earth mining

90% of rare earth processing

93% of rare earth magnet production

In his testimony, Rep. Wittman outlines how China has used unfair trade practices to undercut American producers and threaten supply disruptions. He explains how the SECURE Minerals Act would establish a Strategic Resilience Reserve to stabilize mineral markets, support domestic extraction and processing, and provide financial tools to strengthen U.S. supply chains.

116.title: Deterrence depends not just on announcing arms sales but delivering them.
116.description:
Deterrence depends not just on announcing arms sales but delivering them.
 
President Trump's historic $11 billion arms sale to Taiwan sends a strong signal that reflects America’s commitment to regional security in the Indo-Pacific. With a $21 billion backlog, Congress needs to ensure those commitments translate into real capabilities.
 
Congress must work in a bipartisan manner to strengthen oversight, reduce delays, and ensure Taiwan can rapidly field the capabilities needed to defend its democracy.

| @RepAndyBarr

117.title: Democracy is not an accident, it's a choice, and one that is renewed by every generation.
117.description:
"As America prepares to mark its 250th anniversary next year, and Taiwan approaches 30 years since its first direct presidential election, our democracies remind the entire world of one crucial fact. Democracy is not an accident, it's a choice, and one that is renewed by every generation."

| Chairman @repmoolenaar

118.title: I love the Chinese people. It's just the Chinese Communist Party that's creating all these problems.
118.description:
Reality check: The CCP labels any opposition as “provocation.” Narrative control is central to CCP strategy.

The CCP wants the world to believe Taiwan’s future is already decided, but it's not. The future of Taiwan must be decided peacefully, and free from the CCP's coercion, threats, or force.

119.title: Deterring aggression in the Taiwan Strait is a core U.S. national security interest.
119.description:
If Taiwan falls, the CCP gains control of the first island chain, giving Beijing leverage over global supply chains, maritime commerce, and U.S. economic power.

Chairman Moolenaar has been clear that deterring aggression in the Taiwan Strait is a core U.S. national security interest.

Peace through strength is essential.

120.title: February 17, 2026
120.description:
America’s seed and biotech companies are filled with hardworking Americans.

But when ag and seed companies like Syngenta are bought by CCP-linked entities, it’s no longer just business, it’s leverage.

America must stay in control of its food supply.

121.title: If Taiwan falls, the CCP controls the center of gravity in the Indo-Pacific.
121.description:
If Taiwan falls, the CCP controls the center of gravity in the Indo-Pacific.

At the Atlantic Council, Chairman John Moolenaar made it clear: deterring aggression in the Taiwan Strait is a core U.S. national security interest.

Deterrence must ensure aggression against Taiwan is never “fast, cheap, or successful.”

122.title: Defending Democracy: Why Taiwan Is America’s Front Line in the Indo-Pacific
122.description:
At a major event hosted by the Atlantic Council, Chairman John Moolenaar delivers a powerful address outlining why deterring China's aggression against Taiwan is essential to U.S. national security and economic prosperity.

He emphasizes that Taiwan’s security is directly tied to American jobs, technological leadership, and regional stability. He warns that deterrence must ensure Beijing never believes aggression would be “fast, cheap, or successful.”

As the House Select Committee on China advances its new report, “10 More for Taiwan,” Chairman Moolenaar makes clear: America’s commitment to Taiwan, democratic values, and a free and open Indo-Pacific is bipartisan and unwavering.

123.title: Chairman John Moolenaar at the Atlantic Council | Taiwan, CCP Aggression and U.S. Strategy
123.description:
At an Atlantic Council Front Page event in Washington, DC, Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China outlines why deterring aggression against Taiwan is a core U.S. national security priority.

Discussing the committee’s new report, “10 More for Taiwan,” Moolenaar explains:

- Why Taiwan is vital to U.S. economic and national security
- How Congress is working in a bipartisan way to deter CCP aggression
- The urgency of preparing before 2027
- Strengthening America’s defense industrial base
- Countering CCP information operations and economic coercion

Hosted by the Atlantic Council, this conversation examines how the United States and its allies can preserve peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific through strength and strategic clarity.

124.title: Drones aren’t just flying cameras, they’re potential spies.
124.description:
Drones aren’t just flying cameras, they’re potential spies. 

China dominates the drone market, using tools like DJI drones to monitor farms, ports, and even autonomous vehicle research. Our food systems and tech innovation could be at risk. 

Agriculture is more than crops; it’s critical infrastructure. We must protect it.

125.title: Agriculture isn’t just an industry. It’s infrastructure.
125.description:
Agriculture isn’t just an industry. It’s infrastructure.

If China hacks our grid and telecom systems, what happens if they gain leverage over the systems that feed Americans?

This is why farmland and food production matter to national security.

126.title: FULL HEARING | Lies, Lawfare, and Leverage: CCP’s Gaslighting & Manipulation to Marginalize Taiwan
126.description:
Mr. Julian Ku, Maurice A. Deane Distinguished Professor of Constitutional Law, Hofstra University
Ms. Shirley Kan, Independent Specialist in Indo-Pacific Security Affairs 
Dr. Mira Rapp-Hooper, Visiting Senior Fellow, Brookings Institution

127.title: The CCP is deploying “lawfare” to coerce Taiwan, and intimidate its international supporters.
127.description:
China isn’t just preparing for force against Taiwan, it’s using law as a weapon today.

Prof. Julian Ku warns that the CCP is deploying “lawfare” to coerce Taiwan, intimidate its international supporters, and even target foreign nationals, all below the threshold of armed conflict.

If U.S. policy focuses only on deterring invasion, we miss how the CCP is already changing the status quo.

128.title: The CCP’s “big lie” on Taiwan isn’t just diplomatic spin, it’s lawfare.
128.description:
The CCP’s “big lie” on Taiwan isn’t just diplomatic spin, it’s lawfare. 

UN Resolution 2758 does not determine Taiwan’s status, and it doesn’t even mention Taiwan. 

It’s time the U.S. calls out this truth.

129.title: Bipartisan focus: strong U.S.-Taiwan ties, record arms, trade, and $500B investment.
129.description: The Select Committee is focused on what we can achieve together in a bipartisan manner. U.S. support for Taiwan is strong: record arms sales, the U.S. as the top market for Taiwanese goods, and ongoing trade talks with the potential for $500 billion in investment. Working together is the best way to ensure a secure and prosperous American partnership with Taiwan.

130.title: Rep. Nathaniel Moran Questions Experts on China’s Strategy to Isolate Taiwan
130.description:
Rep. Nathaniel Moran (R-TX) questions experts on Beijing’s ongoing efforts to coerce Taiwan. From economic retaliation to diplomatic pressure and disinformation campaigns, Moran highlights how the Chinese Communist Party is using a broad spectrum of nonmilitary tools to weaken democratic resilience in the Indo-Pacific region.

Witnesses discuss the effectiveness of China’s strategy, including shifts in diplomatic recognition and the vulnerabilities of smaller economies like Taiwan. The hearing also explores ways the United States and its allies can help Taiwan build economic resilience, diversify trade, and maintain security in the region.

131.title: Rep. Zach Nunn Questions Experts on Taiwan’s Allies, Threats, and CCP Coercion
131.description: Rep. Zach Nunn (R-IA) leads a congressional question period examining Taiwan’s most important allies and greatest threats. Experts discuss the U.S.-Taiwan partnership, China’s economic and political coercion, targeted election interference, and strategies to support Taiwan’s resilience without engaging in kinetic conflict. Key topics include agricultural sanctions, defense innovation, and the bipartisan effort to strengthen Taiwan’s security through technology collaboration.

132.title: Rep. Gus Bilirakis Questions Experts on Strengthening Taiwan’s Economic Resilience
132.description: Rep. Gus Bilirakis (R-FL) leads a congressional question period examining strategies to counter China’s economic coercion against Taiwan. Experts discuss how Taiwan can diversify trade, strengthen resilience in key sectors, and participate in emerging international economic initiatives like the AMEC corridor. The discussion also highlights ways Congress can help Taiwan navigate multilateral trade organizations and reduce vulnerability to Beijing’s influence.

133.title: Rep. Carlos Gimenez Questions Experts on China’s Military Ambitions and U.S. Defense Spending
133.description: Rep. Carlos Gimenez (R-FL) questions experts testifying at the Select Committee on China hearing, examining the U.S. response to China’s rising military and economic ambitions. Gimenez emphasizes the importance of actions over words, citing record defense spending as a signal to deter China. He discusses strategic ambiguity in U.S. Taiwan policy, concerns over CCP lawfare, and the risks of neglecting Taiwan in international institutions like the UN.

134.title: Rep. Andy Barr Exposes China’s Lawfare and Threats to Taiwan
134.description:
Rep. Andy Barr (R-KY) examines Beijing’s use of lawfare and gaslighting tactics to undermine Taiwan. Barr highlights key U.S. strategies to deter Chinese aggression, including historic arms sales, the Pacific Deterrence Initiative, and enhanced military-to-military cooperation with Taiwan.

Topics covered in this session:
- Strategic ambiguity vs. enhanced deterrence in U.S. policy toward Taiwan
- $11B historic arms sale to Taiwan, including HIMARS and drones
- Congressional oversight of arms sales and the backlog of $21B in pending deliveries
- Legislation to expedite Taiwan’s defense capabilities, including the Porcupine Act
- Broader U.S. efforts to counter China’s influence in the Indo-Pacific and beyond

Watch as Rep. Barr breaks down how Congress can stand firm against China’s coercion while ensuring Taiwan’s self-defense.

135.title: Chairman Moolenaar Questions Experts on China’s Strategic Pressure and Legal Tactics Against Taiwan
135.description: Chairman Moolenaar leads a congressional question period examining China’s use of lawfare and gaslighting to undermine Taiwan and influence U.S. policy. Experts discuss China’s efforts to distort history, manipulate international law, and limit Taiwan’s relationships with the United States and other countries. The witnesses also explore the implications of Taiwan’s absence from U.S. strategy documents, the importance of clear declaratory policy, and the role of congressional action in safeguarding Taiwan and maintaining regional stability.

136.title: Dr. Mira Rapp-Hooper Testifies | A Consequential Year: China Is Testing U.S. Resolve on Taiwan
136.description:
Dr. Mira Rapp-Hooper of the Brookings Institution delivered urgent testimony on what could be one of the most consequential years in U.S.–China relations.

Dr. Rapp-Hooper detailed how the People’s Republic of China (PRC) is dramatically expanding its use of “peacetime coercion” against Taiwan across military, economic, cyber, and information domains. She warned that Beijing’s objective is clear: to demoralize the Taiwanese people and convince them that maintaining the status quo is untenable.

Despite mounting pressure, Dr. Rapp-Hooper emphasized that the people of Taiwan remain resilient—identifying increasingly as Taiwanese, opposing unification with China, and strongly supporting the status quo. She also highlighted the growing resolve of U.S. allies, including Japan, which has warned that a Chinese attack on Taiwan could threaten its own survival.

However, she cautioned that Taiwan’s security and allied unity depend on consistent, bipartisan U.S. leadership. Dr. Rapp-Hooper raised concerns that Beijing is attempting to shape U.S. Taiwan policy through trade negotiations—seeking to weaken security assistance, delay arms sales, and push for changes in U.S. declaratory policy.

137.title: Shirley Kan Testifies | “Resolution 2758 Is a Lie”
137.description:
Shirley Kan, former Congressional Research Service specialist, delivers urgent testimony on Beijing’s political warfare campaign against Taiwan.

Kan argues that the CCP has been “gaslighting the world” about Taiwan’s status, distorting U.N. General Assembly Resolution 2758, and using coercion and lawfare to advance Xi Jinping’s “national rejuvenation” agenda. She warns that deterrence in the First Island Chain is only as strong as its weakest link and raises concerns about actions in Taiwan’s legislature that could undermine defense preparedness.

138.title: Professor Julian Ku Testifies | China’s Lawfare Against Taiwan: How Beijing Uses Law as a Weapon
138.description:
Hofstra Law Professor Julian Ku warned that Beijing is using “lawfare” to coerce Taiwan, and even foreign nationals, without firing a shot.

Professor Ku’s central argument: the People’s Republic of China is not just using legal claims to justify potential force against Taiwan. It is using law itself as a substitute for force—deploying legal, quasi-legal, and bureaucratic tools to pressure Taiwan, intimidate its leaders, and reshape the international status quo below the threshold of armed conflict.

Watch the full testimony to understand how lawfare has become a central front in the CCP’s strategy toward Taiwan.

139.title: Chairman Moolenaar's Opening Statement: CCP’s “Gaslighting and Gray Zone” Tactics Threaten Taiwan
139.description:
At the Select Committee on China's hearing titled “Lies, Lawfare, and Leverage: The CCP’s Gaslighting and Manipulation to Marginalize Taiwan,” Chairman John Moolenaar delivered opening remarks underscoring bipartisan support for Taiwan and warning of the CCP’s escalating non-military aggression.

Chairman Moolenaar welcomed new Ranking Member Ro Khanna and reaffirmed the Committee’s strong bipartisan tradition in confronting CCP threats. He also recognized Taiwan’s Representative to the United States Alexander Yu and highlighted the Committee’s recent bipartisan “Ten More for Taiwan” report, released alongside $11 billion in approved U.S. arms sales to Taiwan.

The Chairman detailed how the CCP is using economic coercion, cyberattacks, misinformation, legal manipulation, and pressure through international institutions to isolate Taiwan and weaken its democratic institutions—without triggering open conflict. He emphasized that Beijing’s “gray zone” tactics aim to hollow out Taiwan’s democracy long before any military invasion.

As the U.S. approaches its 250th anniversary and Taiwan marks nearly 30 years since its first direct presidential election, Chairman Moolenaar reaffirmed Congress’s bipartisan, unwavering commitment to peace, stability, and Taiwan’s self-determination.

Watch the full opening statement to hear how Congress plans to deter CCP coercion and defend a free and open Indo-Pacific.

140.title: Congress moves to lock in supply chain security—and stop China’s price manipulation.

141.title: China weaponizes minerals. Chairman Moolenaar explains why economic security is national security.

142.title: Building Secure Supply Chains: Chairman Moolenaar on Critical Minerals, Manufacturing, and China
142.description:
Chairman John Moolenaar joins Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg for a fireside discussion on securing America’s critical mineral supply chains.

Chairman Moolenaar outlines Congress’s role in reducing U.S. dependence on China, strengthening domestic mining and processing, codifying executive action into durable law, and working with allies to counter Beijing’s pricing manipulation and supply chain coercion. The conversation highlights Project Vault, permitting reform, workforce development, and why economic security is inseparable from national security in an era of rising geopolitical risk.

143.title: China has changed a lot in the last 25 years, and not for the better. America must continue to lead.

144.title: NVIDIA is selling advanced h200 chips to China. That means fewer chips for American companies.

145.title: Ukraine is a lab for China’s battlefield AI—and human lives are the cost.

146.title: China has a loaded gun pointed at the global economy re: rare-earths and critical minerals.

147.title: “China Has a Loaded Gun” — Chairman Moolenaar on Iran, Rare Earths, and U.S. Dependence on China
147.description:
Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China joins FOX Business' Maria Bartiromo to break down China’s growing role in global instability — from propping up Iran’s economy to weaponizing critical minerals and rare earth supply chains.

Chairman Moolenaar discusses evidence that China’s economic and military support enables Iran and its proxies, including Hamas and Hezbollah, and explains why conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine would be far more difficult to sustain without Beijing’s backing. He also warns that China has repeatedly leveraged rare earth exports to coerce countries like Japan and threaten the United States.

Chairman Moolenaar calls for an all-hands-on-deck strategy, working with allies, the private sector, and Congress, to confront China’s long-term strategy and rebuild American manufacturing and resilience.

148.title: China, AI Warfare, and the Ukraine Battlefield: Chairman Moolenaar Questions Experts
148.description:
Chairman John Moolenaar (R-MI) of the House Select Committee on China questions expert witnesses on how artificial intelligence is already transforming warfare, and how the Chinese Communist Party may seek to use battlefield AI in future conflicts.

Chairman Moolenaar asks how China’s advanced technology ecosystem, combined with its disregard for human life, could shape the use of AI-enabled weapons and autonomous systems. Witnesses describe the war in Ukraine as a “laboratory for modern warfare,” where AI-enabled drones and other systems are being tested in real time, with China closely observing, and learning from, the battlefield.

149.title: FULL HEARING | Trojan Horse: China's Auto Threat to America.
149.description:
The witnesses for the hearing will be:

Ms. Elaine Dezenski, Senior Director and Head of the Center on Economic and Financial Power, Foundation for Defense of Democracies
Mr. Charles Parton OBE, Senior Associate Fellow, Royal United Services Institute
Mr. Peter Ludwig, Co-Founder and Chief Technology Officer, Applied Intuition

150.title: Chinese vehicles pose the same kinds of risks in the physical world as TikTok in the digital world.

151.title: Why would China fight with America? Why not just turn you off?

152.title: China's automotive overcapacity is not an accident. It is incentivized at every level of government.

153.title: Rep. Dusty Johnson Questions Witnesses on Chinese Influence in U.S. Infrastructure
153.description: Rep. Johnson raises concerns about the growing influence of the Chinese Communist Party over critical U.S. infrastructure, from connected vehicles to software systems in transportation. He discusses legislation aimed at protecting American markets and ensuring taxpayer dollars don’t strengthen Chinese technology, emphasizing the need for a comprehensive, bipartisan approach to supply chain vulnerabilities and connected infrastructure.

154.title: Rep. LaHood Presses Experts on China’s Industrial Strategy, USMCA, and U.S. Innovation Threats
154.description:
In this hearing, Rep. Darin LaHood (R-IL) underscores the aggressive nature of the Chinese Communist Party’s 'Made in China' 2025 strategy—highlighting tactics such as intellectual property theft, illegal subsidies, state-owned enterprises, and industrial overcapacity that have hollowed out key U.S. industries from steel and shipbuilding to autos and drones.

Rep. LaHood questions witnesses on how Congress should anticipate China’s next moves, including the implications for the U.S.–Mexico–Canada Agreement (USMCA) and the need to strengthen a “Fortress North America” industrial base. He also presses experts on China’s rapidly accelerating research and development spending and what policies are needed to keep the United States competitive in AI and advanced technology.

155.title: Rep. Young Kim Questions Experts on China’s Threats to American Manufacturing
155.description:
During this hearing, Rep. Young Kim (R-CA) explored the growing risks Chinese firms pose to American manufacturing and North American trade. Topics included:

- Chinese automotive investments in Mexico and potential tariff circumvention under USMCA

- The impact of Chinese vehicles on Mexico’s domestic auto industry

- Threats from substandard, cloned, or malicious electronic parts in U.S. auto and defense systems

- Congressional options to strengthen trade rules and protect economic and national security

Rep. Kim emphasized the need for vigilance in trade enforcement and corporate transparency to safeguard American manufacturing.

156.title: Rep. Newhouse Questions China’s Subsidies and Market Dominance Strategy
156.description:
Rep. Dan Newhouse (R-WA) raises critical questions during a congressional hearing about China’s extensive subsidies and long-term strategy in the auto industry. Experts discuss the stark contrast between U.S. and Chinese incentive structures, the role of state-driven dominance over profit, and what steps the U.S. and its allies can take to counter these practices.

Key topics covered:

- Types and scale of Chinese subsidies for EVs and strategic industries

- Differences between capitalist profit incentives and China’s domination-focused model

- Strategies for the U.S. and allies to protect domestic industries

- The sustainability of China’s state-driven economic approach

This discussion highlights why planning for long-term competitiveness is crucial in the global economy.

157.title: Rep. Ashley Hinson Questions Experts on Chinese Tech Threats to U.S. Transportation
157.description: Rep. Ashley Hinson (R-IA) led a congressional question period examining the national security risks posed by Chinese technology in U.S. transportation infrastructure. Rep. Hinson highlighted concerns over autonomous vehicles using Chinese components, potential cyber vulnerabilities in cars, trucks, and agricultural equipment, and the need for safeguards to protect American supply chains. Experts discussed the dangers of data collection, connected vehicle vulnerabilities, and the implications for national security if foreign actors gain access to critical systems.

158.title: Chairman Moolenaar Questions Experts on China’s Threat to U.S. Auto Industry & National Security
158.description:
Chairman John Moolenaar leads a congressional question period examining the risks posed by China’s automotive strategy to the U.S. economy and national security. Experts discuss the long-term impact on American supply chains, critical components, and related industries, as well as the potential national security threats if Chinese-made vehicles and equipment were widely adopted in the U.S.

Key topics include:

- Loss of U.S. control over critical automotive materials and components

- Risks to small and medium-sized suppliers and the aftermarket

- Broader threats to aerospace, shipbuilding, and advanced manufacturing

- National security concerns involving logistics, trucks, and equipment

- Discussion on potential federal prohibitions on Chinese automotive manufacturers and suppliers

Watch the full discussion to understand the strategic urgency behind protecting America’s industrial base.

159.title: Detroit to Silicon Valley: Why America Must Lead in AI-Powered Vehicles
159.description:
In testimony before the Select Committee, third-generation Detroit Co-Founder and Chief Technology Officer of Applied Intuition Mr. Peter Ludwig ﻿outlines the urgent strategic challenges posed by the People’s Republic of China in the global automotive and AI landscape. 

He traces America’s automotive legacy from the “Arsenal of Democracy” in World War II to the industrial decline driven by unfair Chinese trade practices warning that the next era of competition is centered on AI-defined vehicles.

He details how U.S. innovation can prevail by uniting Detroit’s manufacturing strength with Silicon Valley’s speed, highlighting Applied Intuition’s rapid autonomous vehicle advancements for the U.S. Army. He contrasts this with China’s state-driven industrial strategy, subsidies, and expanding global footprint in low-cost, data-collecting networked vehicles.

His message to Congress is clear: America must act decisively, adopt reciprocal policies, and give the U.S. auto sector the support needed to lead in software-defined vehicles and safeguard national security.

160.title: The Fourth Front: Why Cellular Modules Are China’s Most Immediate Weapon
160.description:
In testimony before Congress, Mr. Charles Parton OBE, Senior Associate Fellow, Royal United Services Institute issues a stark warning: the Chinese Communist Party views itself in a science and technology war with the United States and the most urgent battleground isn’t semiconductors, quantum, or AI. It’s the humble cellular module.

These modules, small components embedded in modern vehicles, energy grids, logistics systems, manufacturing equipment, telecommunications networks, and more, serve as the gateway for data, updates, and control. With China already supplying roughly 70% of the global market and pushing for total dominance, the vulnerabilities are enormous.

This is a comprehensive, urgent call to secure America’s technological backbone before China achieves a dangerous dependency and potential kill switch over vital systems.

161.title: China’s Auto Dumping Exposed: Expert Warns Congress of Industry-Wide Threats
161.description:
Ms. Elaine Dezenski, Senior Director and Head of the Center on Economic and Financial Power, Foundation for Defense of Democracies testifies before the Select Committee about China’s growing threat to the U.S. auto industry and global supply chains.

Her testimony details how China’s state-backed overcapacity, subsidized production, non-market practices, and forced technology transfer are flooding global markets, undermining American workers, and endangering the next generation of automotive innovation.

She outlines the risks to U.S. manufacturers, small and medium-sized suppliers, allied industries in Europe and Asia, and offers recommendations for tariffs, trade enforcement, supply-chain resilience, and coordinated action with partners.

162.title: Chairman Moolenaar's Opening Statement: Warning of CCP Threat to America’s Auto Industry
162.description:
Chairman John Moolenaar opened today’s Select Committee on China hearing with a stark warning: China’s rise as the world’s largest auto exporter isn’t a market success it’s a CCP-driven project that threatens American jobs, supply chains, and national security.

From subsidized EVs flooding global markets to the risks posed by Chinese-made connectivity hardware inside modern vehicles, the Chairman outlined why the U.S. must act now to protect its auto industry, safeguard sensitive data, and keep CCP-controlled technology off American roads.

Watch his full statement and learn how the Committee is working to ensure America’s auto future remains secure, competitive, and free.

163.title: Protecting American Classrooms: Chairman Moolenaar on CCP Influence in Schools
163.description:
Chairman John Moolenaar delivers remarks on critical legislation to protect American students from Chinese Communist Party (CCP) influence in our classrooms.

In this speech, Chairman Moolenaar highlights how the CCP uses exchange programs, curriculum funding, and civil organizations to shape what students learn while hiding the truth about the Cultural Revolution, Tiananmen Square, and the ongoing Uyghur genocide.

The legislation before the House empowers parents, safeguards students, and ensures transparency in education.

164.title: The Courage of Jimmy Lai: Faith, Freedom, and the Fight for Democracy
164.description:
Jimmy Lai is a courageous Hong Konger who has spent decades standing up to the Chinese Communist Party. A devout Catholic, beloved father and husband, and successful businessman, Lai has long defended freedom and democratic values in Hong Kong.

After the 1997 handover, he used his newspaper, Apple Daily, to expose government abuses and champion the rights of Hong Kong’s people. His outspoken commitment to liberty made him a target. Lai was repeatedly charged for participating in peaceful pro-democracy movements, including the 2014 Umbrella Movement and the 2019 protests.

He has been jailed since 2020, facing mistreatment and declining health. Yet his family continues to fight tirelessly for his freedom. The international community, including G7 leaders and President Trump, has urged his release. The House Select Committee on China continues to support Jimmy Lai and introduced a resolution in his honor.

Jimmy Lai’s unwavering stand for justice continues to inspire advocates for democracy around the world. The CCP may believe power comes from fear, but Jimmy Lai shows that courage, truth, and freedom endure.

165.title: Rep. Nathaniel Moran Highlights Smackover Lithium Deposits and Supply Chain Barriers
165.description:
Rep. Nathaniel Moran (TX) leads a critical discussion on the United States’ supply of critical minerals and the ongoing economic strategies of the Chinese Communist Party. During this session, Rep. Moran emphasizes how China is strategically consolidating global control over essential minerals, including lithium, rare earths, and other critical inputs, and the long-term threat this poses to U.S. economic and national security.

Rep. Moran highlights the Smackover formation in northeast Texas, which holds the highest-grade lithium brine resources in North America, and underscores its potential to transform the U.S. into a global leader in lithium production. He questions industry leaders on the barriers slowing domestic development, including permitting delays, capital intensity, and pricing transparency challenges, while exploring how federal policy can accelerate production.

Key topics discussed include:
- China’s predatory tactics in suppressing mineral prices and controlling supply chains
- The economic and strategic importance of lithium and other critical minerals
- How northeast Texas and the broader U.S. can achieve independence from Chinese supply
- The role of tariffs, trade agreements, and the Section 232 investigation in protecting domestic industries
- Opportunities for U.S. innovation and responsible mining to compete globally

This session provides an in-depth look at how U.S. policymakers and industry leaders are working together to ensure the country’s critical minerals security, support domestic industry, and safeguard the nation’s technological and economic future.

166.title: Rep. Carlos Gimenez on America’s Rare Earth Dependence and the China Challenge
166.description:
Rep. Carlos Gimenez led a critical discussion on the United States’ reliance on Chinese rare earth materials and the urgent need for alternative technologies.

Key topics covered in this question period:
- The challenge of competing with China in rare earth production.
- Investment in new magnetic material technologies as alternatives to traditional rare earth magnets.
- U.S. and EU consumption of rare earth magnets and implications for supply chain security.
- Strategies for decoupling from Chinese influence and exploring tariffs to protect U.S. interests.
- The importance of immediate action to secure a reliable and diversified supply of critical minerals.

Experts emphasized that while there are emerging alternatives, solving the rare earth supply chain crisis will require sustained investment, innovation, and global coordination.

167.title: Rep. Dan Newhouse on Critical Mineral Permitting: How the U.S. Can Catch Up to China
167.description:
Rep. Newhouse leads a discussion on the urgent need to reform U.S. federal permitting for critical mineral mining. Witnesses highlight the challenges of lengthy permitting timelines, unpredictable appeals, and the importance of private sector collaboration to accelerate projects.

The hearing also explores:
- National security implications of slow permitting processes
- Environmentally responsible mining in the U.S.
- Alternative technologies reducing dependence on rare Earths
- Leveraging international partnerships to diversify critical mineral supply chains

U.S. competitiveness in critical minerals is at stake, and this hearing emphasizes solutions to strengthen American manufacturing, technology, and national security.

168.title: Rep. Ashley Hinson Questions Experts on China’s Grip Over Critical Minerals Supply Chain
168.description:
In this question period led by Rep. Ashley Hinson, the discussion centers on China’s dominance over critical mineral supply chains and the downstream effects on the U.S. auto industry and other emerging technologies.

Rep. Hinson emphasizes the coercive influence of China in rare earth magnets, lithium, and other critical minerals, highlighting how this impacts American manufacturers, consumer affordability, and global competitiveness. Witnesses discuss the risks of supply chain overreliance on China, strategies to level the playing field, and the importance of developing alternatives domestically or with allied nations.

Key topics include:
- China’s market manipulation during COVID-19 and beyond
- Impacts on the U.S. automotive industry and manufacturing decisions
- Rare earth magnets and their role in AI, robotics, and future technologies
- Steps to diversify critical mineral sources and maintain American competitiveness

This hearing underscores the urgency of strategic action to ensure the U.S. is not dependent on a single foreign power for critical materials vital to innovation and economic security.

169.title: Rep. Neal Dunn Probes Industry Leaders on Domestic Mining, Tax Credits, and Academic Partnerships
169.description:
Rep. Neal Dunn of Florida leads a focused and forward-looking Q&A with executives from America’s leading critical mineral and rare earth companies. Drawing on research at Florida State University, home to the National High Magnetic Field Laboratory, Rep. Dunn highlights innovative work using advanced magnets to separate rare earth elements from decades-old phosphate mine tailings.

The discussion covers:
- New research extracting rare earths and critical minerals from industrial byproducts
- How U.S. companies can partner with universities like FSU and Colorado School of Mines
- Challenges of low-concentration mineral recovery and advanced processing technologies
- Structuring tax credits and incentives to boost domestic mining without reinforcing Chinese dependence
- The industries most at risk if America fails to secure a stable rare earth supply, especially the auto sector

170.title: Rep. Dusty Johnson Pushes for Answers on Permitting Reform and U.S. Competitiveness
170.description:
Rep. Dusty Johnson questions executives from America’s critical mineral sector on whether U.S. government equity stakes in their companies are justified as a response to China’s anti-competitive behavior. Rep. Johnson raises concerns about free market principles, taxpayer exposure, and the precedent set by government ownership of private firms.

Witnesses from MP Materials and Lithium Americas defend these partnerships by pointing to China’s monopoly, distorted pricing, and the need for public-private collaboration to rebuild the U.S. supply chain. They highlight how equity stakes, price floors, and low-cost federal financing have already drawn major private investors and generated significant unrealized gains for taxpayers.

The discussion also dives into the urgent need for permitting reform, with testimony describing multi-year delays, litigation abuse, and the broader challenge of building infrastructure under current NEPA and appeals processes. Executives argue that without legal certainty and streamlined timelines, the U.S. will struggle to compete, attract investment, or build the critical mineral capacity required for national security.

171.title: Rep. Zach Nunn: America Needs a WWII-Style Strategy to Beat China on Critical Minerals
171.description:
Rep. Zach Nunn (R-IA) leads a powerful and urgent line of questioning during the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party’s hearing on critical minerals, rare earths, and U.S. national security.

Nunn lays out a stark picture:
• China refines 85–90% of the world’s rare earth minerals
• Controls 90% of magnet production and 80% of battery production
• Influences major foreign mineral assets—including some tied to U.S. supply chains
• Holds pricing power through control of key global exchanges

From the rare earths needed for F-35 fighter jets to the fertilizer powering Iowa agriculture, Rep. Nunn warns that the United States has built society on resources that China can cut off at will.

In this Q&A exchange, Nunn presses expert witnesses on:
🔹 How the Defense Production Act (DPA) has accelerated U.S. rare earth and lithium development
🔹 Whether DPA must be prioritized in America’s national security strategy
🔹 How U.S. companies can compete with state-backed Chinese subsidies and price manipulation
🔹 The long-term Chinese strategy to suppress global pricing and block new investment
🔹 How a whole-of-nation, WWII-style mobilization could rebuild American mineral independence

Rep. Nunn concludes with a call for national resolve: “This is a 40-year campaign. The Chinese are using economic warfare against us, but America’s innovation can win.”

172.title: Rep. Wittman Presses Industry Leaders: How Fast Can America Rebuild Critical Mineral Supply Chains?
172.description:
Rep. Rob Wittman (R-VA) leads a focused question-and-answer session examining how the United States can close the widening gap with China in critical mineral and rare earth supply chains.

In this exchange, Rep. Wittman asks CEOs from America’s leading rare earth, magnet, and lithium companies how long it will take to rebuild domestic production capacity and what tools, such as price supports, offtake agreements, tariffs, anti-dumping actions, and demand guarantees, could help accelerate investment.

Witnesses from Niron Magnetics, MP Materials, and Lithium Americas detail:
- The capital barriers preventing rapid scale-up
- How predatory Chinese pricing has distorted global markets
- The role of long-term offtake agreements in securing private financing
- The progress already made in U.S. mining, refining, and magnet manufacturing
- The timeline to reach major milestones—including 10,000-ton magnet production capacity and expanded domestic rare earth capabilities

This segment highlights the urgent steps needed to restore U.S. industrial capacity and secure supply chains critical to defense, energy, and advanced manufacturing.

173.title: Private industry leadership with congressional action can anchor a strong rare-earth supply chain.

174.title: Breaking China’s Monopoly: Niron Magnetics CEO on America’s Magnet Innovation
174.description:
Jonathan Rowntree, CEO of Niron Magnetics, testified before the House Select Committee on China on the urgent need to secure the U.S. magnet supply chain and reduce reliance on rare Earth imports. Niron Magnetics manufactures the world’s first commercially scalable, high-powered permanent magnets without any rare Earth elements, using iron and nitrogen, the most abundant elements in the atmosphere.

In his testimony, Rowntree highlighted:
- The strategic risks of China controlling 90%+ of the global rare Earth and magnet market.
- How iron nitride magnets provide a secure, domestic alternative for automotive, defense, consumer electronics, and energy sectors.
- Plans to scale production to 1,500 tons annually by 2027 with a potential second facility reaching 10,000 tons per year.
- Five concrete federal policy recommendations to strengthen the domestic magnet supply chain.

This testimony underscores the critical intersection of national security, industrial innovation, and economic resilience, showing that America can lead in next-generation magnet technology.

175.title: MP Materials CEO Testifies on Securing America’s Rare Earth Supply Chain
175.description:
MP Materials CEO testifies before Congress on securing America’s rare earth supply chain and ending dependence on China. Rare earths may be a small industry, but they power trillions in U.S. economic activity. Everything from electric vehicles, advanced semiconductors, and robotics to AI and defense technologies.

Key points from the testimony:
- Mountain Pass: America’s only scaled rare earth mine and processing facility, rescued from bankruptcy and now a global leader.
- U.S. Investment: Over $1B already invested, with another $1B committed through a transformative public-private partnership with the Pentagon.
- Workforce Growth: From 8 employees in 2017 to nearly 1,000 today across California, Texas, and Nevada.
- Strategic Partnerships: Long-term magnet offtake agreements with major U.S. companies like General Motors and Apple.
- Leveling the Playing Field: Addressing predatory pricing and creating a resilient, domestic supply chain to protect national security.

This testimony highlights how public-private cooperation can restore America’s critical mineral independence and safeguard the economy and defense industries from foreign disruption.

176.title: The Battle for Lithium: Why China’s Pricing Power Threatens U.S. Security
176.description:
In testimony before the House Select Committee on China, Jonathan Evans, President & CEO of Lithium Americas, details how the Chinese Communist Party has used state-backed subsidies, predatory pricing, and control over global benchmarks to dominate the world’s lithium supply chain from mining and processing to battery manufacturing.

Evans outlines why Thacker Pass in Nevada, the largest known lithium resource in the world and a joint venture with General Motors, is vital to America’s economic and national security. Once Phase One is online, the project will:
- Increase U.S. lithium production tenfold
- Supply roughly 20% of domestic lithium demand
- Create high-quality American jobs
- Strengthen secure, transparent, non-Chinese supply chains

He also addresses the challenges posed by China’s 70% share of global lithium chemical processing, 80% share of global battery production, and the CCP’s efforts to suppress western investment by manipulating global pricing benchmarks such as the Shanghai Metals Market and the London Metal Exchange.

Evans calls for:
• Streamlined and predictable permitting
• Timely resolution of appeals
• Federal tools to de-risk early-stage projects
• Expanded DOE financial support
• Policies to ensure transparent market pricing

This testimony underscores why onshoring U.S. lithium production is not optional. It is essential to national security, energy independence, and long-term economic resilience.

177.title: Moolenaar's Opening Statement | Hearing on CCP's Predatory Price Manipulation of Global Rare-Earths
177.description:
In his opening statement, Chairman Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China details how China has spent three decades capturing and weaponizing global supply chains for critical minerals and rare earth elements.

From buying up U.S. technology and tanking global prices to imposing new export restrictions in 2025, the CCP now wields near-total control over materials essential to America’s energy grid, manufacturing base, and defense platforms.

Watch the full statement to understand why U.S. leaders say China’s rare earth monopoly is a “loaded gun” pointed at the global economy, and what must be done to disarm it.

178.title: FULL HEARING | Predatory Pricing: How China Manipulates Global Mineral Prices to Maintain Dominance
178.description:
The witnesses for the hearing will be:

Mr. Jonathan Evans, Chief Executive Office, Lithium Americas
Mr. Matthew Sloustcher, Executive Vice President of Corporate Affairs, MP Materials
Mr. Jonathan Rowntree, Chief Executive Officer, Niron Magnetics
* Additional witnesses to be determined.

179.title: Alibaba, the CCP, and U.S. Cyber Threats — Chairman Moolenaar Says the Risk Is Real
179.description:
Rep. John Moolenaar, Chairman of the House Select Committee China, joins CNBC to break down the escalating controversy surrounding Alibaba, the White House, and alleged tech support for Chinese military cyber operations targeting the United States.

The White House has reportedly circulated intelligence suggesting Alibaba may be aiding China’s military. Alibaba denies the claim as “complete nonsense.” Chairman Moolenaar explains why the CCP’s control over Chinese companies makes the allegations plausible — and why the Pentagon has already labeled Alibaba a “Chinese military company.”

Chairman Moolenaar also weighs in on Middle East dynamics, the Abraham Accords, and the guardrails needed when sharing U.S. technology with partners who maintain ties to Beijing.

180.title: China’s New Rare Earth Threat: Chairman Moolenaar Sounds the Alarm
180.description:
China is developing a new “validated end user” system designed to restrict rare earth minerals and magnet exports to U.S. companies tied to the American military—while fast-tracking shipments to those without defense links.

House Select Committee on China Chairman John Moolenaar joined FOX News to break down:

- How Beijing continues to weaponize its dominance over rare earths and critical minerals
- What President Trump secured in his recent meeting with Xi—and why China is already signaling new restrictions
- Why the U.S. must rebuild domestic mining, refining, and processing capacity
- The Committee’s investigation into Morgan Stanley underwriting an IPO for a Chinese mining firm linked to Uyghur forced labor
- How Wall Street capital is still flowing to companies tied to the CCP’s military and human rights abuses
- What Congress, the administration, and U.S. allies must do to prevent China from exploiting supply-chain vulnerabilities

Chairman Moolenaar also explains the push for a U.S. strategic minerals reserve, stronger guardrails on American investments, and why ordinary investors may unknowingly be funding companies connected to slave labor and the Chinese military.

181.title: China controls the minerals that power America — it’s time to take back our supply chains.

182.title: China’s Stranglehold on Critical Minerals: How the CCP Endangers America’s Supply Chains
182.description:
We’re at a crossroads in the competition with the Chinese Communist Party over critical minerals — the resources that power our military, technology, and everyday products.

A new bipartisan report from the House Select Committee on China reveals how Beijing manipulates global mineral markets to control prices, undermine American companies, and threaten U.S. national security.

From rare earth elements like Samarium—vital for defense systems—to the broader supply chain for critical materials, China’s market dominance leaves America vulnerable.

This video explains what’s at stake, what the Select Committee uncovered, and the 12 key policy recommendations to secure our nation’s mineral supply chains and rebuild an American-centric mining industry.

📘 Read the full report and press release here: https://selectcommitteeontheccp.house.gov/media/press-releases/bipartisan-investigation-reveals-how-the-ccp-manipulates-the-critical-minerals-market

183.title: “David vs. Goliath”: Chairman Moolenaar on Michigan’s Fight Against a CCP-Linked Battery Plant
183.description:
Michigan Congressman John Moolenaar, Chairman of the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, joins WOOD TV’s To the Point with host Rick Albin to discuss:

- The collapse of the controversial Goshen battery plant in Mecosta County
- Concerns over CCP-linked companies receiving taxpayer funding
- The bipartisan effort to protect U.S. farmland from foreign adversaries
- China’s military ambitions near Taiwan and its impact on global security
- Efforts to reshore manufacturing and reduce dependence on Chinese supply chains

Chairman Moolenaar explains how local citizens stood up to protect their community, why America must strengthen economic and national security, and how the Select Committee is exposing the CCP’s growing global influence.

184.title: America's commitment to peace, stability, & Taiwan's self-determination is bipartisan & unwavering.

185.title: Chairman Moolenaar: TikTok Sale, China’s Role in Fentanyl Crisis, and U.S.–China Tensions
185.description:
Rep. John Moolenaar (R-MI), chairman of the House Select Committee on China, joins CBS 'Face The Nation' with Margaret Brennan to discuss U.S. efforts to confront China’s influence — from the TikTok divestment deal to the fentanyl crisis and the importance of protecting American data and national security.

Rep. Moolenaar explains why the CCP’s control over TikTok’s algorithm poses a risk to U.S. users, how Congress plans to oversee the app’s ownership transition, and why he believes China’s role in fentanyl trafficking must be confronted directly.

🔔 Subscribe for more interviews and updates on U.S.–China relations and national security.

186.title: The CCP’s espionage is a threat to every democracy. #ccp #china

187.title: Chairman Moolenaar Warns UK: Take China Espionage Threat Seriously
187.description:
House Select Committee on China Chairman John Moolenaar (R-MI) joins SkyNews to discuss concerns over the UK’s handling of alleged Chinese espionage cases and the proposed “mega-embassy” in London.

In this interview, Chairman Moolenaar outlines why the CCP’s espionage and influence operations pose a direct threat to the sovereignty of free nations, and why the U.S. and its allies must take a unified, decisive stand against the CCP’s malign activities.

188.title: China isn’t just competing for markets—it’s reshaping the rules of the international order.

189.title: It’s time to revoke China’s “normal” trade status. Free trade is for free nations, not the CCP.

190.title: Inside the U.S.–China Tech War: Chips, AI, and National Security
190.description:
House Select Committee on China Chairman John Moolenaar joins the Hudson Institute to discuss America’s strategic competition with the Chinese Communist Party — from rare earths and critical minerals to AI chips, biotechnology, and supply chain security.

Chairman Moolenaar outlines how the CCP is using economic leverage, technology theft, and “debt-trap diplomacy” to advance its global ambitions — and how Congress is responding through bipartisan action on trade, technology, and national security.

Watch Chairman Moolenaar’s full conversation for insight into how the U.S. can strengthen its defenses, rebuild key industries, and safeguard freedom in the face of the CCP’s growing aggression.

🔔 Subscribe for more updates from the House Select Committee on the CCP.
📺 Learn more: https://selectcommitteeontheccp.house.gov/

191.title: Chairman John Moolenaar: “Xi Jinping Is Funding Putin’s War—China Is Not a Reliable Ally”
191.description:
House Select Committee on China Chairman Rep. John Moolenaar (R-MI) joins The Hill to discuss China’s growing alliance with Russia, the CCP's economic coercion tactics, and what America must do to protect its national and economic security.

Chairman Moolenaar warns that Xi Jinping is directly funding Putin’s war in Ukraine through technology transfers and dual-use materials — a partnership that threatens global peace and stability. He also calls for the United States to rebuild its industrial and military base, reduce dependence on China, and strengthen alliances to deter further aggression in Asia and beyond.

192.title: Chairman Moolenaar Speaks Out on China’s Systematic Religious Oppression
192.description:
Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on the CCP delivers powerful testimony before the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom on China’s escalating campaign against religious freedom. Highlighting the persecution of Uyghur Muslims, Christians, Falun Gong practitioners, and other faith groups, Chairman Moolenaar exposes the CCP’s systematic effort to replace God with the state.

He calls on the international community to recognize the human rights abuses and religious oppression under Xi Jinping’s regime and emphasizes the global implications of China’s war on faith.

📌 Topics Covered:

Religious persecution in China

Uyghur genocide and forced assimilation

Crackdown on underground churches and faith leaders

Surveillance and suppression of religious communities

Global implications of CCP control over faith

#ReligiousFreedom #China #CCP #HumanRights #Uyghur #ChristianPersecution #ChinaSelect

193.title: Chairman Moolenaar: Faith, Freedom, and Standing Up to the CCP
193.description:
At the Hudson Institute, Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party delivers a powerful address on defending freedom, faith, and America’s technological leadership.

Chairman Moolenaar outlines a bold new strategy—the Rolling Technical Threshold (RTT)—to ensure the Chinese Communist Party can never catch up to U.S. innovation in artificial intelligence and advanced technology. He emphasizes that America’s openness and ingenuity must never again be weaponized to strengthen authoritarian control.

From the persecution of Chinese pastors and Uyghur Muslims to the CCP’s use of Western technology for repression, this speech makes clear: the defense of freedom begins with clarity, unity, and resolve.

Key themes:

Standing with those persecuted for their faith in China

The U.S.–China contest for technological and moral leadership

The Rolling Technical Threshold: keeping the CCP dependent, not dominant

Strengthening America’s supply chains, semiconductor production, and alliances

#China #CCP #AI #Technology #Freedom #Faith #HudsonInstitute #JohnMoolenaar #SelectCommittee

194.title: Chairman John Moolenaar: China’s Rare Earth Ban Is a ‘Sputnik Moment’ for America
194.description:
Republican Congressman John Moolenaar, Chairman of the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, joined CNBC to respond to China’s latest economic and technological moves — from rare earth export bans to restrictions on U.S. chips.

In this interview, Chairman Moolenaar warns that Beijing’s actions amount to a “Sputnik moment” for the United States, calling for “all hands on deck” to secure America’s technological edge and economic independence. 

He discusses:
China’s crackdown on NVIDIA chip sales and rare earth exports

The global semiconductor race and what it means for U.S. allies like Japan and the Netherlands

Why he believes China’s economy operates under full control of the Communist Party

How the U.S. and its partners can build a “free world tech alliance” to counter Beijing’s influence

#JohnMoolenaar #ChinaCommittee #Semiconductors #RareEarths #AI #NVIDIA #USChinaRelations #EconomicSecurity #TechCompetition #SelectCommitteeOnChina

235.description:
Video summary of Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party and House Committee on Education and Workforce joint report: "Chinese Communist Party on the Quad: How American Taxpayers and Universities Fund the CCP's Advanced Military and Technological Research"

Following a year-long investigation, Chairman John Moolenaar (R-MI) of the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party and Chairwoman Virginia Foxx (R-NC) of the House Education and Workforce Committee uncovered that hundreds of millions of dollars in U.S. federal research funding over the last decade has contributed to China’s technological advancements and military modernization. Through nearly 9,000 joint research publications, funded by the Department of Defense or the Intelligence Community, the lawmakers discovered that Americans worked with Chinese researchers on strategic technology research, much of which has military applications. These papers covered topics like high-performance explosives, tracking of targets, and drone operation networks, nuclear and high-energy physics, artificial intelligence, quantum technology, and hypersonics – the kind of technology that the Chinese military could use against the U.S. military in the event of a conflict.

In six case studies, covering research institutions including UCLA and U.C. Berkeley, the lawmakers illustrate how the People's Republic of China defense and security establishment benefits from technological advances developed by federally funded researchers. Those six researchers leveraged expertise, applied knowledge, and practical capabilities developed through and during years of receiving federal funding to the PRC’s advantage, helping the PRC achieve advancements in fourth- generation nuclear weapons technology, artificial intelligence, advanced lasers, graphene semiconductors, and robotics.

The lawmakers also uncovered that US-Chinese joint education institutes like U.C. Berkeley’s partnership with Tsinghua University, and the University of Pittsburgh's partnership with Sichuan University, serve as conduits for transferring critical U.S. technologies and expertise to China, including to entities linked to China’s defense machine and the security apparatus it uses to facilitate human rights abuses.

259.title: Microsoft/G42 AI Partnership EXPLAINED - Potential Benefits & Risks for U.S. Technological Security
259.description:
In April, Microsoft announced a $1.5 billion partnership with G42. 

While the deal could benefit American business & relations with the United Arab Emirates, it could also open a backdoor for U.S. technology & dollars to flow to the Chinese Communist Party’s (CCP) surveillance state & military research.

Chairman John Moolenaar (R-MI) of the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party and Chairman Michael McCaul (R-TX) of the House Committee on Foreign Affairs requested a classified briefing from the Biden administration as the chairmen remain concerned that without robust protections, sensitive U.S.-origin technology transferred as part of the Microsoft-G42 partnership could end up the CCP’s hands.

Chairmen Moolenaar and McCaul write, “It is vital we do all we can to limit the PRC's [People’s Republic of China] malign influence around the world, including in the Middle East... we support your efforts to work hand in glove with U.S. companies like Microsoft to strengthen our dominance in AI; however, we must also be clear-eyed about the risks posed by transferring our most critical AI technology particularly when it comes to countries where the PRC is active.”

The lawmakers continue, “Given the ties between the PRC and G42 as well as PRC’s continued interests in the UAE, we ask that the National Intelligence Council prepare an official Intelligence Community assessment on the ties between G42, including its subsidiaries and affiliates, to the Chinese Communist Party, the People’s Liberation Army, or any part of the PRC’s apparatus.”

Background:

In January, the Select Committee outlined some of G42’s most problematic connections with Chinese military companies, state-owned enterprises, and Chinese intelligence services. According to documents reviewed by the Committee, G42’s CEO Peng Xiao operates and is affiliated with an expansive network of UAE and People’s Republic of China-based companies that develop dual-use technologies and materially support PRC military-civil fusion and human rights abuses. Following the Select Committee’s inquiry, G42 announced that it severed its relationships with some problematic Chinese entities. Then in April, Microsoft announced a $1.5 billion partnership with G42, furthering the UAE’s aspirations to be a global AI leader.

However, last month, UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan traveled to China and described AI as an area of deeper PRC – UAE collaboration. As a result, lawmakers remain concerned that key American technology could end up the CCP’s hands, originating from Microsoft’s partnership with G42.

280.title: Moolenaar, Krishnamoorthi Request Chinese Doping Investigation Ahead of Paris Olympics
280.description:
Chairman John Moolenaar (R-MI) and Ranking Member Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) of the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party called on the U.S. Department of Justice and the International Olympic Committee to launch a formal inquiry, seeking immediate action and transparency following the World’s Anti-Doping Agency’s (WADA) decision to allow Chinese swimmers to participate in the 2021 Olympics after testing positive for illegal substances. The letter was also signed by Reps. Carlos Gimenez (R-FL) and Rep. Andre Carson (D-IN).
 
Ahead of the 2021 Tokyo Olympics, 23 Chinese swimmers tested positive for a prohibited substance, trimetazidine, but continued to swim after the Chinese anti-doping agency delayed reporting these samples and the World Anti-Doping Agency refused to intervene. Despite U.S. and global anti-doping officials presenting strong evidence to WADA, officials neglected to open an independent review at that time.
 
Curiously, WADA also received $2 million in excess funds from the Chinese government that year. Some of the Chinese swimmers who were doping proceeded to medal in events, calling into question the validity of the Olympic Games and the credibility of the International Olympic Committee. Now that the 2024 Paris Summer Olympics are less than 100 days away, it is imperative for the International Olympic Committee to hold WADA accountable and ensure Chinese athletes who test positive for prohibited substances are not allowed to compete.
 
In the letter to the Attorney General and FBI Director, the lawmakers write, “This scandal raises serious legal, ethical, and competitive concerns and may constitute a broader state-sponsored strategy by the People’s Republic of China (PRC) to unfairly compete at the Olympic Games in ways Russia has previously done… It is imperative to assess whether these alleged doping practices were state-sponsored, which could warrant further diplomatic measures by the United States and the international community. Furthermore, with less than 100 days until the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris, understanding the full scope of the scandal is critical in ensuring our U.S. athletes are competing in a fair competition.”
 
In a separate inquiry to the International Olympic Committee, the lawmakers write, “The deeply troubling revelation that nearly two dozen Chinese swimmers, including multiple Olympic medalists, tested positive for a prohibited substance months before the Tokyo Games, yet were still permitted to compete, represents a significant breach of these foundational principles and a profound injustice to clean athletes around the world… How the IOC responds to this scandal will directly affect this summer’s Olympic games and their promise of fair play that unites athletes from around the globe.”
 
The lawmakers seek a briefing from the FBI and Attorney General by June 5, 2024.

291.title: INVESTIGATION FINDINGS: U.S. Financial Institutions Funneled Billions into Blacklisted Chinese Firms
291.description:
Chairman Mike Gallagher (R-WI) and Ranking Member Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) of the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) today unveiled the findings of their bipartisan investigation into the world’s foremost index provider, MSCI., and the world’s largest asset manager, BlackRock. The investigation also included a canvass of the broader U.S. financial industry. The lawmakers found that index providers and asset managers, on an industry-wide basis, facilitated investment of more than $6.5 billion to 63 PRC companies that the United States government has red-flagged or blacklisted for advancing People's Republic of China (PRC) military capabilities or supporting its human rights abuses. 

American financial institutions are facilitating investments worth billions of dollars in People’s Republic of China (PRC) companies that advance the PRC’s military ambitions and perpetrate the Chinese Communist Party’s (CCP) human rights abuses. The Select Committee investigated two companies—the world’s foremost index provider, MSCI, and the world’s largest asset manager, BlackRock—and canvassed the broader financial industry to understand the full scope of the problem.

The results are shocking. In 2023:

Major financial institutions provided $6.5 billion to 63 PRC companies that the U.S. government has blacklisted or otherwise red-flagged because they advance the PRC’s military capabilities or support the CCP’s human rights abuses.
 MSCI indexes alone channeled $3.7 billion to these entities.
BlackRock invested at least $1.9 billion in these companies.

These companies develop advanced fighter jets and nuclear weapons for the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) and create the technology used to perpetrate the ongoing genocide against the Uyghur people. What may surprise many Americans is that the activity by U.S. financial institutions described below is not illegal. It is time for Congress to act. 

Index providers and asset managers channel funds to these red-flagged companies. MSCI and other index providers claim to mirror financial markets with their products, but they rely on subjective determinations about the PRC market and individual securities to build an index. MSCI’s subjective market determinations lead it to include problematic PRC companies’ securities in its index offerings. By adding a red-flagged company’s security to an index, index providers effectively give that company a stamp of approval, signaling the company is investable and its securities hold a certain value.

Asset managers like BlackRock then channel investments to the securities on an index. They decide the goals, strategy, and duties associated with their investment funds. They write prospectuses that provide the ability to deviate from indexes and add new, un-indexed red-flagged companies’ securities to their funds. Perhaps unsurprisingly, they do not adequately describe the CCP’s authoritarianism and human rights abuses in their descriptions of investment products as they facilitate investment in these problematic PRC companies—in some cases, they do not mention them at all.

BlackRock and MSCI are not alone—a cross-industry review revealed that other major index providers and asset managers funnel billions of dollars to the same red-flagged entities.

The existing regulations prohibiting investment in certain Chinese companies because of national security risks or human rights violations are insufficient. Congress must act to restrict U.S. investment in entities tied, directly or indirectly, to the PLA, critical technology sectors, or forced labor and genocide. Congress specifically should pass legislation to:

Restrict investment in companies blacklisted by the U.S. government, including subsidiaries, affiliates, parents, and holding companies.
Require U.S. public companies to disclose key risks related to the PRC.
Ensure the U.S. financial system is resilient to PRC market uncertainty.

Short of such action, billions of dollars of Americans’ life savings will continue funding the PRC’s military and human rights abuses, including the Uyghur genocide. 

Head to our website to read the full report.

299.title: Select Committee Investigates: The CCP's Role in the Fentanyl Crisis
299.description:
Following a months-long investigation, Chairman Mike Gallagher (R-WI) and Ranking Member Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) of the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party revealed their findings of the Chinese Communist Party’s role in the deadly fentanyl epidemic that has killed hundreds of thousands of Americans.

The fentanyl crisis is one of the most horrific disasters that America has ever faced. On average, fentanyl kills over 200 Americans daily, the equivalent of a packed Boeing 737 crashing every single day. Fentanyl is the leading cause of death for Americans aged 18-45 and a leading cause in the historic drop in American life expectancy. It has led to millions more suffering from addiction, and the destruction of countless families and communities. Beyond the United States, fentanyl and other mass-produced synthetic narcotics from the People’s Republic of China (PRC) are devastating nations around the world. It is truly a global crisis. 

The PRC, under the leadership of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP), is the ultimate geographic source of the fentanyl crisis. Companies in China produce nearly all of illicit fentanyl precursors, the key ingredients that drive the global illicit fentanyl trade. The House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party (Select Committee) launched an investigation to better understand the role of the CCP in the fentanyl crisis.

This investigation involved delving deep into public PRC websites, analyzing PRC government documents, acquiring over 37,000 unique data points of PRC companies selling narcotics online through web scraping and data analytics, undercover communications with PRC drug trafficking companies, and consultations with experts in the public and private sectors, among other steps.

The Select Committee's investigation has established that the PRC government, under the control of the CCP:      

Directly subsidizes the manufacturing and export of illicit fentanyl materials and other synthetic narcotics through tax rebates. Many of these substances are illegal under the PRC’s own laws and have no known legal use worldwide. Like its export tax rebates for legitimate goods, the CCP’s subsidies of illegal drugs incentivizes international synthetic drug sales from the PRC. The CCP never disclosed this program.

Gave monetary grants and awards to companies openly trafficking illicit fentanyl materials and other synthetic narcotics. There are even examples of some of these companies enjoying site visits from provincial PRC government officials who complimented them for their impact on the provincial economy.

Holds ownership interest in several PRC companies tied to drug trafficking. This includes a PRC government prison connected to human rights abuses owning a drug trafficking chemical company and a publicly traded PRC company hosting thousands of instances of open drug trafficking on its sites.

 Fails to prosecute fentanyl and precursor manufacturers. Rather than investigating drug traffickers, PRC security services have not cooperated with U.S. law enforcement, and have even notified targets of U.S. investigations when they received requests for assistance.

Allows the open sale of fentanyl precursors and other illicit materials on the extensively monitored and controlled PRC internet. A review of just seven e-commerce sites found over 31,000 instances of PRC companies selling illicit chemicals with obvious ties to drug trafficking. Undercover communications with PRC drug trafficking companies (whose identities were provided to U.S. law enforcement) revealed an eagerness to engage in clearly illicit drug sales with no fear of reprisal.

Censors content about domestic drug sales, but leaves export-focused narcotics content untouched. The PRC has censorship triggers for domestic drug sales (e.g., “fentanyl + cash on delivery”), but no such triggers exist to monitor or prevent the export of illicit narcotics out of the PRC.

Strategically and economically benefits from the fentanyl crisis. The fentanyl crisis has helped CCP-tied Chinese organized criminal groups become the world’s premier money launderers, enriched the PRC’s chemical industry, and has had a devastating impact on Americans.

While the PRC government publicly acknowledged in November 2023 that the trafficking of fentanyl precursors and other illicit narcotics materials in the manner described above is illegal under Chinese law, the Select Committee found thousands of PRC companies openly selling these illicit materials on the Chinese internet—the most heavily surveilled country-wide network in the world. The CCP runs the most advanced techno-totalitarian state in human history that “leave[s] criminals with nowhere to hide” and has the means to stop illicit fentanyl materials manufacturers, yet it has failed to pursue flagrant violations of its own laws.
